definition_zh: n. 喷出；弹出；驱逐；弹射（逃生）
definition_en: the act of forcing something or someone out; escape from an aircraft by an explosive seat
core_image: 超声室屏幕上标着一个百分比，医生用笔点着它解释心脏每次收缩泵出的血量比例；座椅上方的黄色拉环与「弹射座椅」标牌；一封信被推到桌沿外
scene: 医院超声室里，屏幕上标着一个百分比，医生指着它说这是心脏每次收缩泵出的血量比例。 The report listed an ejection fraction of sixty per cent.
sceneCN: 这里 ejection 指「用突然推力把东西弄出去的动作」（第 1 个义项：喷出；弹出），医学上特指心脏泵血；句意是报告列出射血分数为百分之六十。图中可辨识物件：超声屏幕、百分比、医生的笔。

pos.zh: 喷出；弹出；驱逐；弹射（逃生）

senses.title: The act of forcing out
senses.definition: the act of forcing something out with a sudden push
senses.definitionCN: （名词）用突然推力把东西弄出去的动作
senses.example: The report listed an ejection fraction of sixty per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出射血分数为百分之六十。
senses.why: A percentage marked on an ultrasound screen with a pen tip pointing at it.
senses.whyCN: 超声屏幕上标着一个百分比，笔尖正指着它。

senses.title: The act of expelling
senses.definition: the act of forcing a person to leave a place
senses.definitionCN: （名词）强迫某人离开某地的行为
senses.example: The letter announced his ejection from the club after the third warning.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信宣布，第三次警告之后他将被逐出俱乐部。
senses.why: A formal letter pushed to the edge of a desk beside a membership card.
senses.whyCN: 一封正式信函被推到桌沿，旁边放着一张会员卡。

senses.title: Escape by ejection seat
senses.definition: the escape of a pilot from an aircraft by an explosive seat
senses.definitionCN: （名词）飞行员借爆炸座椅逃离飞机
senses.example: The yellow handle above the seat is the last step before ejection.
senses.exampleCN: 座椅上方那个黄色拉环，是弹射之前的最后一步。
senses.why: A yellow loop above a cockpit seat beside a printed warning plate.
senses.whyCN: 驾驶舱座椅上方一个黄色拉环，旁边一块印着警告的标牌。

intro.en: Ejection is Latin ejectio, a throwing out, built on ejectus from ejicere, which joins ex- meaning out to jacere meaning to throw.
intro.cn: ejection 就是拉丁语 ejectio（扔出去这件事），建立在 ejectus 之上，而 ejectus 来自 ejicere，它把 ex-（向外）与 jacere（投掷）结合。

items.en: Latin jacere means to throw.
items.cn: 拉丁语 jacere 意为投掷。

items.en: Adding ex- gives ejicere, to throw out.
items.cn: 加 ex- 构成 ejicere，意为扔出去。

items.en: The noun ejectio names a throwing out.
items.cn: 名词 ejectio 指扔出去这件事。

items.en: English took ejection in the 15C for expulsion from a place or office.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪借用 ejection，指从某地或某职位被赶出。

items.en: Doctors used ejection for the blood pushed out of the heart.
items.cn: 医生用 ejection 指心脏泵出的血液。

items.en: Ejection seat became the standard term for cockpit escape.
items.cn: ejection seat 成为座舱逃生的标准术语。

note.en: Ejection, rejection and injection all end in -jection, from Latin jacere, to throw; the prefix decides out, back or in.
note.cn: ejection、rejection 与 injection 都以 -jection 结尾，来自拉丁语 jacere（投掷）；前缀决定是向外、向后还是向内。

dict_mnemonic.text: ejection ＝ e-（向外）＋ ject（投掷，拉丁 jacere）＋ -ion（名词后缀，表动作）＝「往外扔这件事」。动词 eject 加 -ion 就成名词，同规律：reject → rejection 拒绝、inject → injection 注射、project → projection 投射、object → objection 反对。三个高频术语直接背：ejection seat 弹射座椅、ejection fraction 射血分数（心脏每次收缩泵出的血量比例）、ejection from a club 被逐出俱乐部。近义 expulsion 偏「开除、驱逐」，emission 偏「排放气体或光」，discharge 偏「排出、释放、出院」。注意 ejection 可数（一次弹射／一次驱逐），但射血分数语境里通常单数。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）＋ jacere（投掷）→ ejectus（被扔出的）＋ -ion → ejection（喷出；驱逐）

definition_zh: 高架渠；输水道；导水管
definition_en: a structure that carries water over a long distance, especially a bridge-like channel
core_image: 跨谷的石桥上驮着一条水路：水在高处流过山谷
scene: 古城郊外，石拱桥高耸，桥顶的水槽直通城里的喷泉。 The Roman aqueduct still carries water to the fountain.
sceneCN: 这里 aqueduct 是「输水道、高架渠」（第 1 个义项：引水的桥式建筑）；句意为：罗马时代的输水道仍把水送到喷泉。

derivatives.zh: 同根词（aqu- 水），义为「水的；水生的」
同根词（duc- 引导），义为「导管；管道」
同根近形词，义为「导管；水道」
同构复合词，义为「高架桥」

senses.title: A bridge-like water channel
senses.definition: a raised structure with a channel for carrying water across a valley
senses.definitionCN: 带水槽的高架结构，跨谷输水
senses.example: The aqueduct spans the valley on stone arches.
senses.exampleCN: 输水道以石拱跨越山谷。
senses.why: The root ducere means to lead: the structure leads water where it must go.
senses.whyCN: 词根 ducere 意为引导：这种结构把水引向该去的地方。

senses.title: A conduit or pipe system
senses.definition: any pipe or channel built to transport water
senses.definitionCN: 为输水而修建的管道或水槽
senses.example: A modern aqueduct supplies the whole city.
senses.exampleCN: 一条现代化输水道供给全市用水。
senses.why: Leading water needs only a channel; the material may change.
senses.whyCN: 引水只需要一条通道，材质可以变化。

senses.title: An ancient Roman engineering work
senses.definition: one of the famous Roman structures that supplied cities with water
senses.definitionCN: 为城市供水的著名罗马建筑之一
senses.example: Tourists photograph the aqueduct at Segovia.
senses.exampleCN: 游客在塞哥维亚拍摄输水道。
senses.why: Rome built the model case, so the word recalls it.
senses.whyCN: 罗马建造了典范工程，这个词便让人想起它。

senses.title: An anatomy duct
senses.definition: a small natural passage carrying fluid in the body
senses.definitionCN: 体内输送液体的小型天然管道
senses.example: The aqueduct of the brain channels cerebrospinal fluid.
senses.exampleCN: 大脑导水管输送脑脊液。
senses.why: Bodies also lead water, so anatomy borrowed the engineering word.
senses.whyCN: 身体也要引水，解剖学便借用了工程术语。

senses.title: A long-distance supply line
senses.definition: a large-scale channel moving water from a distant source to cities or farms
senses.definitionCN: 把水从远处水源输往城市或农田的大型渠道
senses.example: The state aqueduct feeds farms in the dry valley.
senses.exampleCN: 州立输水道滋养干旱山谷中的农田。
senses.why: Leading water across regions extends the original crossing.
senses.whyCN: 跨区域引水是「跨越」一词的延伸。

senses.title: A symbol of engineering skill
senses.definition: an object used figuratively to represent great civil engineering
senses.definitionCN: 在比喻中代表伟大土木工程的事物
senses.example: The dam became the aqueduct of our age.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝成了我们这个时代的输水道。
senses.why: The perfect model case becomes the measuring stick for others.
senses.whyCN: 典范案例成为衡量其他工程的标尺。

senses.title: A lifeline of a city
senses.definition: the essential route without which a settlement cannot survive
senses.definitionCN: 定居点赖以生存的必需通道
senses.example: Cutting the aqueduct would starve the town.
senses.exampleCN: 切断输水道将令城镇陷入绝境。
senses.why: Because led water is led life, the channel becomes a lifeline.
senses.whyCN: 引来的既是水也是命，渠道因此成为生命线。

senses.title: A heritage monument
senses.definition: a preserved ancient structure valued as cultural heritage
senses.definitionCN: 作为文化遗产被保存的古代建筑
senses.example: The aqueduct was restored last decade.
senses.exampleCN: 输水道在上个十年得到修复。
senses.why: What once led water now leads memory and tourism.
senses.whyCN: 昔日引水，今日引来的记忆与游人。

intro.en: Aqueduct joins Latin aqua, water, and ductus, a leading, from ducere, to lead.
intro.cn: aqueduct 由拉丁语 aqua（水）与 ductus（引导）复合而成，后者来自 ducere（引导）。

items.en: The reconstructed roots *akwa- (water) and *deuk- (to lead) underlie both parts.
items.cn: 重构词根 *akwa-（水）与 *deuk-（引导）分别支撑两个部分。

items.en: Aqua meant water; ducere meant to lead or draw.
items.cn: aqua 意为水；ducere 意为引导、牵引。

items.en: Aquaeductus named the channels Rome built to lead water into cities.
items.cn: aquaeductus 指罗马为城市引水修建的渠道。

items.en: English took aqueduct in the sixteenth century, partly through French, partly from Latin.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪经法语或直接从拉丁语借入 aqueduct。

items.en: It now covers ancient monuments, modern supply channels, and anatomical ducts.
items.cn: 如今涵盖古迹、现代输水渠道与解剖学导管。

note.en: Aqueduct combines two famous roots and is often confused with viaduct.
note.cn: aqueduct 复合了两个著名词根，且常与 viaduct 混淆。

entries.definition: a bridge carrying a road or railway across a valley

entries.definition: a channel or pipe for water or cables
entries.definitionCN: 导管；管道

entries.definition: water, or a light blue-green color
entries.definitionCN: 水；水绿色

entries.definition: a man-made waterway for boats or irrigation
entries.definitionCN: 运河；灌溉渠

entries.definition: a passage along which water flows
entries.definitionCN: 水道；渠道

entries.definition: a line of pipes carrying liquid or gas

normalIntro.en: Split aqueduct into aqua plus duct and it builds itself.
normalIntro.cn: 把 aqueduct 拆成 aqua + duct，它就自己拼出来了。

normal.en: aqua (water) + duct (lead): a channel that leads water.
normal.cn: aqua（水）+ duct（引导）：引水的通道。

normal.en: Same duct root as conduct, product, reduce.
normal.cn: 与 conduct、product、reduce 同属 duct 词根。

normal.en: Same aqua root as aquarium, aquatic, aquamarine.
normal.cn: 与 aquarium、aquatic、aquamarine 同属 aqua 词根。

normal.en: Contrast: a viaduct carries vehicles, an aqueduct carries water.
normal.cn: 对照记：viaduct 载车，aqueduct 载水。

normal.en: Image anchor: stone arches carrying a river on their backs.
normal.cn: 意象锚点：石拱背上驮着一条河。

abstract.en: A stone giant drinking from one river and pouring into a fountain.
abstract.cn: 石头巨人从一条河喝水，向一座喷泉倾倒。

abstract.en: A tightrope walker balancing a long water pipe across a canyon.
abstract.cn: 走钢丝的人扛着长水管走过峡谷。

abstract.en: Aqueduct sounds like 'aqua duck': a duck leading water in a line.
abstract.cn: aqueduct 听着像 aqua duck：一只鸭子领着水排队走。

examples.en: The city built a new aqueduct from the mountain reservoir.
examples.cn: 该市从山区水库新建了一条输水道。

examples.en: Aqueducts made Roman cities possible.
examples.cn: 输水道使罗马城市的繁荣成为可能。

examples.en: Engineers inspect the aqueduct every spring.
examples.cn: 工程师每年春天检修输水道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿奎 duck」——阿奎赶着鸭群引水过桥，谐音仅助记，词源仍是 aqua + duct。

root: 拉丁复合词根：aqu-（水，如 aquarium）+ duct-（引导，如 conduct），aqueduct 即「引水之物」；罗马人的 aquaeductus 指引水入城的渠道。

sensesIntro.en: From leading water across a valley, aqueduct extends to pipe systems, Roman monuments, anatomical ducts, regional supply lines, symbols of engineering, urban lifelines, and heritage sites.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「跨谷引水」出发，aqueduct 延伸到管道系统、罗马古迹、解剖导管、区域供水线、工程象征、城市生命线与历史遗迹。

branches.cn: 历史的一面：罗马工程与遗产

definition_zh: 壁画；墙画；（作定语）墙壁的；墙面大型显示画面
definition_en: a painting made directly on a wall; also used attributively for things fixed to or forming a wall
core_image: 一整面高墙被画面完全覆盖，颜料直接吃进灰泥里，人站在墙前像站在画中
scene: 美术馆走廊的尽头有一整面高墙，工作人员正刷上最后一层保护漆， The restorer climbs a scaffold to clean the mural above the doorway.
sceneCN: 这里 mural 指「直接画在墙面上的整幅绘画」（第 1 个义项：墙面绘画）；句意为修复师爬上脚手架，清理门上方那幅壁画。图中可辨识物件：高墙、脚手架、修复刷与整幅画面。

senses.title: A painting made on a wall
senses.titleCN: 直接画在墙面上的绘画
senses.definition: a picture painted directly onto a wall surface
senses.definitionCN: 直接绘制在墙面上的一幅画
senses.example: The mural covers the whole eastern wall of the library.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅壁画覆盖了图书馆东侧的整面墙。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin muralis, 'of a wall', so the painting is named after the surface it belongs to rather than after a frame.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 muralis「墙的」，所以画是以它所属的墙面命名，而不是以画框命名。

senses.title: A public artwork on an outdoor wall
senses.titleCN: 户外墙面上的公共艺术作品
senses.definition: a large painting on an exterior wall, often made for a neighbourhood or a cause
senses.definitionCN: 画在外墙上的大型绘画，常为社区或某项议题而作
senses.example: A mural of migrating birds now runs along the school fence.
senses.exampleCN: 一幅候鸟壁画如今沿学校围墙铺开。
senses.why: When the wall faces a street, the picture addresses everyone who passes, so the sense shifts from private decoration to public statement.
senses.whyCN: 当墙面朝向街道，画就在向每个路过的人说话，词义便从私人装饰转向公共表达。

senses.title: A wall-sized picture inside a building
senses.titleCN: 建筑内部占满墙面的画
senses.definition: a very large picture covering an interior wall, as in a lobby, hotel or restaurant
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖室内墙面的大幅画作，常见于大堂、酒店或餐馆
senses.example: The hotel lobby mural depicts the city before the railway arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店大堂的壁画描绘了铁路通车前的城市。
senses.why: The same surface logic holds indoors: the picture is sized to the wall and becomes part of the room rather than an object standing in it.
senses.whyCN: 同样的墙面逻辑也适用于室内：画按墙的尺寸展开，成为房间的一部分，而不是立在房间里的物件。

senses.title: Of or fixed to a wall (attributive)
senses.titleCN: 墙壁的；固定于墙上的（定语用法）
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean belonging to, attached to or forming a wall
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示属于墙壁、附着于墙或构成墙的
senses.example: The chapel is known for its mural decoration and painted ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小教堂以墙面装饰和彩绘天顶闻名。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the word: the Latin adjective described anything that pertained to a wall, and English kept that use beside the noun.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层：拉丁形容词本指任何与墙有关之物，英语把这个用法与名词义保留在一起。

senses.title: Of the wall of a body cavity (anatomy)
senses.definition: in medicine, relating to the wall of an organ or cavity rather than to its contents
senses.definitionCN: 医学中，指器官或腔体的壁，而非其内部内容物
senses.example: The scan showed a mural thickening in the lower intestine.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示下段肠道有肠壁增厚。
senses.why: Anatomy borrowed the Latin sense directly: whatever sits in or belongs to a wall is mural, so a clot attached to a heart wall is a mural thrombus.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学直接借用了拉丁义：凡是位于壁上或属于壁的都叫 mural，因此附着在心脏壁上的血栓称为壁性血栓。

senses.title: A wall-mounted interactive image
senses.definition: a digital image or interactive surface mounted flat on a wall, often in a gallery or control room
senses.definitionCN: 平贴在墙上的数字图像或互动界面，常见于展馆或控制室
senses.example: Visitors can drag a timeline across the digital mural in the entrance hall.
senses.exampleCN: 参观者可以在入口大厅的数字壁画上拖动时间轴。
senses.why: Digital displays inherit the two defining traits of a mural, being large and fixed to a wall, and the name follows the form rather than the pigment.
senses.whyCN: 数字显示屏继承了壁画的两个核心特征——尺幅大、固定在墙上——名称便随形态延续，而不随颜料延续。

senses.title: A wall-sized array of screens
senses.titleCN: 由多块屏幕拼成的墙面显示阵列
senses.definition: a large video wall built from many tiled displays and treated as one continuous image
senses.definitionCN: 由多块拼接显示屏构成、当作一幅连续画面使用的大型屏幕墙
senses.example: The operations centre monitors the grid on a six-metre video mural.
senses.exampleCN: 运营中心在一块六米长的屏幕墙上监控电网。
senses.why: Once many screens are aligned without visible seams, the result looks like one painted surface, which is why the older word is applied to the newer wall.
senses.whyCN: 当许多屏幕无缝对齐，整体看起来就像一整块绘制的表面，旧词因此被用在这种新墙上。

senses.title: A surrounding field of images
senses.titleCN: 环绕观看者的整片图像
senses.definition: a continuous visual field that surrounds viewers and replaces the ordinary walls of a space
senses.definitionCN: 环绕观看者、替代空间普通墙面的连续视觉场
senses.example: The installation wraps the audience in a slow-moving mural of ocean light.
senses.exampleCN: 这件装置用一片缓慢流动的海光壁画把观众包围起来。
senses.why: The figurative step is small: if a mural can cover a wall, enough murals can cover every wall, and the picture becomes the room itself.
senses.whyCN: 这一步比喻跨度很小：既然一幅壁画能覆盖一面墙，足够多的壁画就能覆盖所有墙面，画便成了房间本身。

intro.en: Mural comes from Latin muralis 'of a wall', built on murus 'wall' with the adjective suffix -alis. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mural 来自拉丁语 muralis「墙的」，由 murus「墙」加形容词后缀 -alis 构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Murus meant 'wall', especially the wall of a house or a city. Its deeper origin is not established, and the links sometimes proposed to other Indo-European wall words are hypotheses rather than demonstrated derivations.
items.cn: murus 意为「墙」，尤指房屋或城墙。其更深来源未得到证明；有人把它与其他印欧语系的「墙」词联系起来，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The suffix -alis 'pertaining to' produced muralis, an adjective for anything that belonged to or stood on a wall.
items.cn: 后缀 -alis「属于……的」构成 muralis，指任何属于墙或立于墙上的事物。

items.en: English received mural in the fifteenth century as an adjective describing walled structures and wall decoration.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪接受了 mural，用作描述有墙结构及墙面装饰的形容词。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the phrase mural painting was shortened to the noun mural, and the picture rather than the wall became the thing named.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，「墙面绘画」这一短语缩略为名词，被命名的事物从墙面转到了画本身。

items.en: In the twentieth century, especially through Mexican and American mural movements, the noun came to name large public works painted on exterior walls.
items.cn: 在 20 世纪，尤其经由墨西哥与美国的壁画运动，这个名词开始指画在外墙上的大型公共作品。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin source of murus is unsettled, so any Indo-European root offered for it is a reconstruction rather than a witnessed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：murus 在拉丁语之前的来源并无定论，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构形式，而非实际书证。

note.en: The first group contains words that sound close to mural but come from other roots; the second contains words for wall pictures that differ in technique, scale or intent.
note.cn: 第一组是读音接近但词根不同的词；第二组指墙面图画，但在技法、尺度或意图上有别。

entries.definition: Concerned with right and wrong behaviour; it comes from Latin mos 'custom', not from murus 'wall'.
entries.definitionCN: 关于行为是非的；来自拉丁 mos「习俗」，与 murus「墙」无关。

entries.definition: The spirit and confidence of a group; it shares the mos root and has nothing to do with walls.
entries.definitionCN: 群体的士气与信心；同属 mos 词根，与墙无关。

entries.definition: Simply the plural of mural, not a separate term.
entries.definitionCN: 只是 mural 的复数形式，并非另一个词。

entries.definition: A wall painting made on fresh lime plaster, so the pigment sets into the wall itself; fresco names the method, mural names the surface.
entries.definitionCN: 画在新鲜石灰灰泥上的墙画，颜料随灰泥固化进入墙体；fresco 指技法，mural 指墙面。

entries.definition: A neutral cover term for any picture on a wall, whether painted wet or dry.
entries.definitionCN: 任何墙面绘画的中性统称，无论湿画还是干画。

entries.definition: Words or tags written or sprayed on walls; usually text-based and unauthorized rather than a composed picture.
entries.definitionCN: 写在或喷在墙上的文字与标记；通常以文字为主、未经许可，不是完整构图的画。

entries.definition: Art made in public spaces by any method; a mural is one form of street art, not its equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 以任何方式在公共空间创作的艺术；壁画只是街头艺术的一种形式，并不等同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, the real word family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: Murus 'wall' + -alis 'pertaining to' = a picture that belongs to the wall.
normal.cn: murus「墙」+ -alis「属于……的」= 属于墙的画。

normal.en: The same -al ending marks global, local and natural, all adjectives of belonging.
normal.cn: 同一个 -al 结尾也见于表示「全球的」「本地的」「自然的」等形容词。

normal.en: A mural is not hung on a wall; it is the wall's own skin.
normal.cn: 壁画不是挂在墙上，而是墙自己的一层皮。

normal.en: Museums label a large wall picture a mural rather than a canvas, because the wall is its support.
normal.cn: 博物馆把大幅墙面画称作 mural 而非画布，因为墙才是它的载体。

normal.en: Street murals often carry a community's signature, which is why the word travels with public art.
normal.cn: 街头壁画常带着社区的署名，因此这个词常与公共艺术同行。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose every riser has been painted by a different hand, so the climb reads as one long story.
abstract.cn: 想象一架楼梯，每一级竖面都由不同的人画过，整段攀登读起来像一个长故事。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that remembers the hands that painted it, layer over layer, until the plaster itself is memory.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙记得画过它的每一双手，一层叠一层，直到灰泥本身成为记忆。

abstract.en: Picture a city speaking through its outer skin instead of through its voice.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市不靠声音，而靠外皮说话。

examples.en: The museum commissioned a mural for the blank wall beside the main staircase.
examples.cn: 博物馆委托艺术家在主楼梯旁的空白墙面上创作一幅壁画。

examples.en: Years of rain had faded the outdoor mural to pale outlines.
examples.cn: 多年雨水把户外壁画冲刷成淡淡的轮廓。

examples.en: The new station uses a digital mural to show the river's changing level.
examples.cn: 新车站用一幅数字壁画显示河水水位的变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「缪若」听成「描墙」——拿笔在墙上描，描满一整面，就是壁画。murus 是墙，-alis 是「属于……的」，墙所属的画自然叫 mural。

root: 拉丁 murus「墙」加形容词后缀 -alis「属于……的」构成 muralis「墙的」；英语先用其形容词义，后由「墙面绘画」这一短语缩略成名词「壁画」。murus 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，相关印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the painted wall itself, then move outward to public street works, interior wall pictures, the wall-based adjective, anatomy, wall-mounted digital images, tiled screen walls and finally a field of images that surrounds the viewer.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从画在墙上的画本身出发，向外扩展到街头公共作品、室内墙面画、表示「墙的」形容词义、解剖学用法、墙面数字画面、拼接屏幕墙，最后是环绕观看者的整片图像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a high wall whose whole surface has become a single picture, so the boundary of a room turns into a frame.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整面高墙的整个表面变成一幅画，房间的边界因此成了画框。

branches.en: THE WALL ITSELF: the core sense is a picture that belongs to the wall rather than to a frame.
branches.cn: 墙本身：核心义是一幅属于墙面而非属于画框的画。

branches.en: INSIDE AND OUTSIDE: the same wall-sized picture serves a street audience or an interior room.
branches.cn: 墙内与墙外：同样尺幅的墙面画，可以服务街头观众，也可以服务室内房间。

branches.en: THE WALL AS QUALIFIER: the adjective sense keeps the plain meaning 'of a wall', even when medicine narrows it to an organ wall.
branches.cn: 墙作限定语：形容词义保留「墙的」这一朴素含义，医学只是把它收窄到器官壁。

branches.en: WALL-BOUND MEDIA: screens inherit the mural's fixed, wall-sized character, first as one interactive surface and then as a tiled array.
branches.cn: 固定在墙上的媒介：屏幕继承了壁画固定、以墙为尺幅的特征，先是一整块互动面，再是拼接阵列。

branches.en: A FIELD RATHER THAN AN OBJECT: the idea widens until the picture surrounds the viewer and the room itself becomes the work.
branches.cn: 从物件到场：这一观念不断放宽，直到画面包围观看者，房间本身成为作品。

intro.en: Mural is built from one Latin noun, one Latin suffix and a small English family, so it can be read piece by piece.
intro.cn: mural 由一个拉丁名词、一个拉丁后缀和一小族英语派生词构成，可以逐块读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin murus 'wall' gives mural, muralis and the medical adjective; the suffix -alis marks belonging, and English added -ist and -ism for people and movements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 murus「墙」衍生出 mural、muralis 及医学形容词；后缀 -alis 表示归属，英语再加表示从事者的后缀与表示做法或运动的后缀。

items.meaning: wall, especially a house or city wall
items.example: The noun supplies the surface at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供了这个词的核心表面。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun of place into an adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把表示场所的名词变成表示归属的形容词。

items.example: Latin used the adjective for anything attached to a wall.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语用这个形容词指任何附着于墙的事物。

items.meaning: a wall painting; of a wall
items.example: English kept both the noun and the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留了名词与形容词用法。

items.example: The suffix marks the person who does the work.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记从事这项工作的人。

items.example: A muralist works on the wall itself, not on canvas.
items.exampleCN: 壁画家直接在墙上工作，而不是在画布上。

items.example: The suffix turns an activity into a movement or a style.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一种活动变成运动或风格。

items.meaning: the practice or movement of painting murals
items.meaningCN: 壁画创作实践或壁画运动
items.example: Muralism became a public art programme in the twentieth century.
items.exampleCN: 壁画主义在 20 世纪成为一项公共艺术计划。

derivatives.structure: mural + -ism (practice or movement suffix, from Latin -ismus)
derivatives.meaning: the practice or movement of mural painting
derivatives.meaningCN: 壁画创作实践或壁画运动

definition_zh: 侵蚀；磨蚀；逐渐削弱；使逐渐丧失
definition_en: to wear away rock or soil gradually, or to weaken and reduce something such as value, trust or rights
core_image: 海浪日夜拍打崖壁，把松软岩层一点点掏空，崖顶草地不断向后退
scene: 海浪日夜拍打崖壁，把松软的岩层一点点掏空，崖顶的草地正往后退。 Waves erode the soft cliff a little more each winter.
sceneCN: 这里 erode 指「（自然营力）逐渐磨掉、掏空岩体」（第 1 个义项：侵蚀岩石或土壤）；句意为海浪每个冬天都多啃掉一点这段软崖。可辨识物件：崖壁、浪花、掏空的岩层、崖顶草地。

senses.title: Wear away rock or soil
senses.definition: of water, wind or ice: to wear away rock or soil gradually
senses.definitionCN: 指水、风或冰逐渐磨掉岩石或土壤
senses.example: Waves erode the soft cliff a little more each winter.
senses.exampleCN: 海浪每个冬天都多啃掉一点这段软崖。
senses.why: The transitive verb puts the agent first: waves erode cliffs.
senses.whyCN: 及物动词把营力放在前面：波浪侵蚀崖壁。

senses.title: Be worn away
senses.definition: to be worn away gradually by natural forces
senses.definitionCN: 指受自然营力逐渐磨蚀
senses.example: The old shore erodes faster than the headland.
senses.exampleCN: 旧岸比岬角侵蚀得更快。
senses.why: The intransitive verb lets the surface itself be the subject.
senses.whyCN: 不及物动词让表面本身成为主语。

senses.title: Reduce value or profit
senses.definition: to reduce money, profit or advantage gradually
senses.definitionCN: 指逐渐减少金钱、利润或优势
senses.example: Freight costs erode the profit on each crate.
senses.exampleCN: 运费侵蚀着每箱货的利润。
senses.why: Costs remove profit as water removes rock.
senses.whyCN: 成本移除利润，正如水移除岩石。

senses.title: Weaken confidence or trust
senses.definition: to make confidence, trust or reputation gradually weaker
senses.definitionCN: 指使信心、信任或声誉逐渐减弱
senses.example: Repeated delays eroded public trust in the project.
senses.exampleCN: 一再延误削弱了公众对这个项目的信任。
senses.why: Repeated failure removes trust grain by grain.
senses.whyCN: 反复失败一粒一粒地移除信任。

senses.title: Wear down rights or standards
senses.definition: to weaken rights, freedoms or standards by small steps
senses.definitionCN: 指以渐进方式削弱权利、自由或准则
senses.example: Emergency powers eroded the right to assemble.
senses.exampleCN: 紧急权力侵蚀了集会权。
senses.why: Small legal steps remove rights the way waves remove a cliff.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的小步移除权利，正如波浪移除崖壁。

senses.title: Wear away chemically
senses.definition: of acid: to eat into a surface such as enamel or metal
senses.definitionCN: 指酸对牙釉质、金属等表面的侵蚀
senses.example: Stomach acid can erode tooth enamel.
senses.exampleCN: 胃酸会侵蚀牙釉质。
senses.why: Acid attacks enamel at the chemical scale.
senses.whyCN: 酸在化学尺度上攻击牙釉质。

senses.title: Cut into the land
senses.definition: of a river: to cut a channel or valley into the land
senses.definitionCN: 指河流在地表切出河道或河谷
senses.example: The river erodes a narrow gorge through the limestone.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河在石灰岩中切出一条窄峡谷。
senses.why: A river removes bed and bank, which is how it cuts a channel.
senses.whyCN: 河流移除河床与河岸，正是这样切出河道。

senses.title: Gradually weaken an advantage or base
senses.definition: to reduce an advantage, majority or base by small degrees
senses.definitionCN: 指逐步减少优势、多数席位或基础
senses.example: New competitors eroded the firm's lead.
senses.exampleCN: 新的竞争者削弱了这家公司的领先地位。
senses.why: Competition removes a lead by small degrees.
senses.whyCN: 竞争一点一点地移除领先优势。

intro.en: Erode comes from Latin erodere 'to gnaw out', the same verb that stands behind erosion.
intro.cn: erode 来自拉丁 erodere「啃出、蚀去」，与 erosion 出自同一动词。

items.en: Rodere 'to gnaw' is the root verb; its pre-Latin origin is not established, and suggested Indo-European links are hypotheses.
items.cn: rodere「啃」是词根动词；它在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，所提出的印欧关联均属假说。

items.en: E- 'out' plus rodere gave erodere 'to gnaw away, eat into', used of animals, acids and ulcers before it was used of land.
items.cn: e-「出」加 rodere 构成 erodere「啃掉、蚀入」，在用于土地之前，先用于动物、酸与溃疡。

items.en: English took the verb from French eroder or directly from Latin in the seventeenth century, at first in medical and chemical contexts.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪经法语 eroder 或直接自拉丁语借入该动词，最初用于医学与化学语境。

items.en: In the nineteenth century erode became the everyday geological verb paired with erosion, and it was applied to rivers, glaciers and waves.
items.cn: 在十九世纪，erode 成为与 erosion 配对的地质日常动词，用于河流、冰川与波浪。

items.en: From the twentieth century the verb spread to money, trust and rights, where the image of slow removal still governs the meaning.
items.cn: 从二十世纪起，这个动词扩展到金钱、信任与权利，其中「缓慢移除」的形象仍主导词义。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the deeper origin of rodere is unsettled. The route from Latin erodere to English erode is established, though the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：rodere 的更深来源没有定论。从拉丁 erodere 到英语 erode 的路径是确定的，但确切首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds verbs that look like erode but have other roots; group two holds verbs of wearing away and weakening.
note.cn: 第一组是外形近似但词根不同的动词；第二组是表示磨损与削弱的动词。

entries.definition: To escape or avoid, from e- 'out' plus vadere 'go'; it shares the prefix and the sound but not the 'gnaw' root.
entries.definitionCN: 指逃脱或避开，来自 e-「出」加 vadere「走」；共享前缀与读音，但没有「啃」的词根。

entries.definition: To burst out, from e- plus rumpere 'break'; volcanic eruptions are the opposite of slow wearing.
entries.definitionCN: 指爆发，来自 e- 加 rumpere「破裂」；火山喷发与缓慢磨蚀正相反。

entries.definition: To eat away chemically, from cor- 'thoroughly' plus rodere; it is a true relative that stresses chemical attack.
entries.definitionCN: 指化学性蚀去，来自 cor-「彻底」加 rodere；它是真正的同族词，强调化学侵蚀。

entries.definition: To rub out or delete, from eradere 'to scrape out', built on the same rodere root; it means removing marks, not wearing land.
entries.definitionCN: 指擦掉或删除，来自 eradere「刮出」，建立在同一 rodere 词根上；它指去除痕迹，而非磨蚀土地。

entries.definition: The everyday equivalent for slow removal by friction or weather; erode is its technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指摩擦或风化造成缓慢移除的日常说法；erode 是其技术对应词。

entries.definition: To rub or scrape a surface, from ab- 'away' plus radere 'scrape'; it stresses contact friction.
entries.definitionCN: 指摩擦或刮削表面，来自 ab-「离开」加 radere「刮」；强调接触摩擦。

entries.definition: To carry off by water, as soil from a field; erode is the geological term for the same action.
entries.definitionCN: 指被水冲走，如田里的土；erode 是同一动作的地质术语。

entries.definition: To weaken something gradually, often secretly, from under- plus mine; it is the figurative cousin of erode.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐渐、常为暗中地削弱，来自 under- 加 mine；它是 erode 的比喻近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real verb family and the real abstract collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的动词词族与真实的抽象搭配。

normal.en: E- 'out' plus rodere 'gnaw': to gnaw material out of a surface.
normal.cn: e-「出」加 rodere「啃」：把材料从表面啃出去。

normal.en: The family runs erode, erosion, erosive, erosional, erodible, erosivity.
normal.cn: 词族包括 erode、erosion、erosive、erosional、erodible、erosivity。

normal.en: The same root appears in corrode, erase and rodent.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 corrode、erase 与 rodent 中。

normal.en: Fixed abstract phrases: erode confidence, erode trust, erode margins, erode rights.
normal.cn: 固定抽象搭配：削弱信心、侵蚀信任、侵蚀利润、侵蚀权利。

normal.en: In landscape writing erode takes a direct object: rivers erode valleys, waves erode cliffs.
normal.cn: 在地貌写作中 erode 直接带宾语：河流侵蚀河谷，海浪侵蚀崖壁。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose every step is a little lower than last year.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯，每一级都比去年低一点。

abstract.en: Picture a promise rubbed thin by being repeated too often.
abstract.cn: 想象一个承诺因反复重申而被磨薄。

abstract.en: Picture a wave that never breaks anything, only carries one grain away.
abstract.cn: 想象一道浪从不打碎什么，只带走一粒沙。

examples.en: The river has eroded a channel thirty metres deep.
examples.cn: 这条河已切出三十米深的河道。

examples.en: Rising costs eroded the profit margin on the product.
examples.cn: 成本上升侵蚀了该产品的利润率。

examples.en: Repeated scandals eroded voters' trust in the council.
examples.cn: 接连的丑闻削弱了选民对议会的信任。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one verb from the cliff to the balance sheet: a force removes material, then the same slow removal appears as a channel, as lost profit, as weakened trust, as narrowed rights, as etched enamel and as a shrinking lead.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个动词从崖壁走到账本：某种力量带走物质，同一种缓慢移除随后表现为河道、流失的利润、被削弱的信任、被收窄的权利、被蚀出的牙釉质与缩小的领先。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: surf hollowing the base of a cliff while the grass above moves inland.
core.cn: 核心意象：浪把崖脚掏空，上方的草地向内陆移动。

branches.en: ACT AND BE ACTED ON: the same verb works with an agent or with the surface itself.
branches.cn: 作用与受作用：同一动词既可带施事，也可描述表面本身。

branches.en: CUTTING DOWN: a river erodes a gorge by removing bed and bank.
branches.cn: 向下切割：河流靠移除河床与河岸切出峡谷。

branches.en: CHEMICAL TOOTH: acid erodes enamel by the same logic at a smaller scale.
branches.cn: 化学的牙齿：酸在更小尺度上按同一逻辑侵蚀牙釉质。

branches.en: MONEY AND TRUST: costs and delays remove value the way water removes rock.
branches.cn: 金钱与信任：成本与延误会像水搬走岩石那样搬走价值。

branches.en: RIGHTS AND LEADS: small steps remove what was once solid.
branches.cn: 权利与领先：小步侵蚀移除曾经稳固之物。

definition_zh: 审理；裁决；裁定；担任裁判
definition_en: to hear and decide a case or dispute officially, or to act as the judge of a competition
core_image: 一张摆着卷宗的桌子，桌后的人敲下木槌，把两边争持的线画成一条
scene: 两家公司为一块地的边界争了三年，最后把材料交到仲裁庭。 The tribunal will adjudicate the boundary dispute next month.
sceneCN: 这里 adjudicate 指由第三方正式审理并作出裁决（第 1 个义项：审理案件）；句意为仲裁庭将在下个月裁决这起边界争议。

senses.title: Hear and decide a case
senses.definition: to examine a legal case and give an official decision on it
senses.definitionCN: 审查法律案件并作出正式决定
senses.example: The court agreed to adjudicate the bankruptcy case.
senses.exampleCN: 法院同意审理这起破产案件。
senses.why: The Latin verb joined 'to' with 'to judge': the judge is brought to the matter so that a decision can be fixed.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词把「向」和「审判」连在一起：把审判者带到事情面前，好让决定被固定下来。

senses.title: Settle a dispute
senses.definition: to settle a disagreement between parties by an authoritative decision
senses.definitionCN: 以权威决定解决各方之间的分歧
senses.example: An independent panel was appointed to adjudicate the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 一个独立小组被指定来裁决这场争议。
senses.why: A dispute is two claims pulling in opposite directions; adjudication cuts the line between them.
senses.whyCN: 争议是两个主张朝相反方向拉扯；裁决在它们之间划下界线。

senses.title: Rule on a claim or right
senses.definition: to decide whether a claim, right or objection is valid
senses.definitionCN: 判定某项主张、权利或异议是否成立
senses.example: The agency adjudicated her claim for compensation.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构裁定她的赔偿主张。
senses.why: A claim is a demand held up for recognition; the judge either confirms it or lets it fall.
senses.whyCN: 主张是一个举起来等待承认的要求；审判者要么确认它，要么让它落下。

senses.title: Act as a judge
senses.definition: to serve in the role of judge at a hearing or formal proceeding
senses.definitionCN: 在听证或正式程序中担任审判者角色
senses.example: A retired justice will adjudicate at the final hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 一位退休法官将在最终听证会上担任裁判。
senses.why: Here the verb names the office rather than the single act: the person is placed in the judging seat.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词命名的是职位而不是单次动作：这个人被安置在审判席上。

senses.title: Judge a competition
senses.definition: to assess entries or performances in a contest and decide the winners
senses.definitionCN: 评比比赛中的作品或表演并决定优胜者
senses.example: Three composers were invited to adjudicate the piano contest.
senses.exampleCN: 三位作曲家受邀来评定这场钢琴比赛。
senses.why: The contest is a field of rival claims; the adjudicator turns many claims into one ranking.
senses.whyCN: 比赛是一片相互竞争的主张；裁判把许多主张变成一个名次。

senses.title: Award a prize officially
senses.definition: to officially decide that a prize or title belongs to a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 正式判定某项奖赏或头衔归某人所有
senses.example: The committee adjudicated the scholarship to the youngest applicant.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会把奖学金判给了最年轻的申请人。
senses.why: The decision transfers a thing from the group to one holder, which is the judging act at its most concrete.
senses.whyCN: 这个决定把一件东西从集体转到某个持有者手里，这是审判行为最具体的形态。

senses.title: Rule in a bankruptcy or tribunal
senses.definition: to determine the legal status of a debtor, claim or proceeding in a tribunal
senses.definitionCN: 在审裁机构中确定债务人、债权或程序的法律地位
senses.example: The tribunal adjudicated the company insolvent.
senses.exampleCN: 审裁庭裁定该公司破产。
senses.why: A status is not a thing one can see; it exists only after an authority declares it, so the verb creates the status it names.
senses.whyCN: 地位不是肉眼可见之物；它只在权威宣布之后才存在，因此这个动词创造了它所命名的地位。

senses.title: Give an official ruling
senses.definition: to issue a formal ruling that binds the parties, whether or not they accept it
senses.definitionCN: 发布对各方有约束力的正式裁定，无论他们是否接受
senses.example: The board adjudicated that the contract was void.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会裁定该合同无效。
senses.why: The last step is the binding word: once spoken by the right body, the decision stops being an opinion and becomes an order.
senses.whyCN: 最后一步是有约束力的话语：一旦由正确的机构说出，决定就不再是意见，而成为命令。

intro.en: Adjudicate is a Latin legal verb built from 'to' and 'to judge'. Its family includes judge, judicial and prejudice.
intro.cn: adjudicate 是一个由「向」和「审判」构成的拉丁法律动词。它的同族词包括 judge、judicial 与 prejudice。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 17c. from Latin adjudicare, first in legal writing and later in competition language.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪从拉丁语 adjudicare 借入这个动词，先用于法律文本，后来进入比赛用语。

items.en: Adjudicare meant 'to give by judgement, award, decide'. The prefix ad- 'to' shows the judge directing the decision toward a person or thing.
items.cn: adjudicare 意为「凭审判给予、判给、裁定」。前缀 ad-「向」表示审判者把决定指向某人或某物。

items.en: Judicare 'to judge' comes from judex, a compound of jus 'law, right' and dicere 'to say, declare'.
items.cn: judicare「审判」来自 judex，由 jus「法、权利」与 dicere「说、宣告」复合而成。

items.en: The phrase jus dicere, literally 'to say the law', is the origin of the judge's role: the law is spoken into a particular case.
items.cn: 短语 jus dicere 字面意为「说出法律」，这正是审判者角色的来源：法律被说进具体案件之中。

items.en: The noun adjudication and the agent adjudicator keep the courtroom image, while sport and music contests extend it to any ranked decision.
items.cn: 名词 adjudication 与施动者 adjudicator 保留法庭意象，而体育与音乐比赛把它扩展到任何排名决定。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin judging root; the near-meaning group names people or acts that decide disputes.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁「审判」词根；近义组列出决定争议的人或行为。
