definition_zh: 国内生产总值；一国境内一定时期内生产的最终产品与服务总值
definition_en: the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a given period
core_image: 会议桌上摊开一年的账本，几个人把全国做成的每一件事折算成一个总数
scene: 统计局的会议室里，几个人把一年的产出逐项加总，想用一张表说明整个国家到底做出了多少东西。 The report compares gross domestic product across two decades.
sceneCN: 这里 gross domestic product 指「一国境内一定时期内生产的最终产品与服务总值」（第 1 个义项：按市场价格衡量的境内最终产出总量）；句意为这份报告比较了二十年的国内生产总值。图中可辨识物件：摊开的账本、加总表、计算器、墙上地图。

collocations.zh: 国内生产总值平减指数

senses.title: The total value of domestic output
senses.definition: the market value of all final goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a period
senses.definitionCN: 在一定时期内、于一国国境之内生产的所有最终商品与服务的市场价值
senses.example: The report compares gross domestic product across two decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告比较了二十年的国内生产总值。
senses.why: Each word limits the measure: gross counts everything before allowances, domestic fixes the border, and product names what is made rather than what is earned.
senses.whyCN: 每个词都在限定这个度量：gross 指扣除之前的全部，domestic 固定国境，product 指被做出来的东西而非被赚到的收入。

senses.title: Nominal GDP
senses.definition: output valued at the prices of the year in which it was produced, without removing price change
senses.definitionCN: 按生产当年的价格估值的产出，未剔除价格变动
senses.example: Nominal gross domestic product jumped simply because fuel cost more.
senses.exampleCN: 名义国内生产总值猛增，只是因为燃料更贵了。
senses.why: When current prices are used, a price rise looks like more output, which is why the nominal measure needs a real counterpart.
senses.whyCN: 用当年价格计算时，涨价看起来就像产出增加，因此名义度量需要一个「实际」的对应物。

senses.title: Real GDP
senses.definition: output valued at the prices of a fixed base year, so that only changes in quantity are shown
senses.definitionCN: 按某一固定基年的价格估值的产出，从而只显示数量的变化
senses.example: Real gross domestic product barely moved once inflation was stripped out.
senses.exampleCN: 剔除通胀之后，实际国内生产总值几乎没动。
senses.why: Holding prices constant isolates the physical increase, and the word real here means 'in constant prices', not 'actual'.
senses.whyCN: 把价格固定住就分离出实物的增加，这里的 real 意为「按不变价格」，而不是「真实的」。

senses.title: GDP per head
senses.definition: total output divided by the population, used as a rough measure of average income
senses.definitionCN: 总产出按人口平均分摊，用作平均收入的粗略度量
senses.example: Gross domestic product per capita doubled in a generation.
senses.exampleCN: 人均国内生产总值在一代人的时间里翻了一倍。
senses.why: A total says nothing about how many people share it, so the phrase is routinely divided by population.
senses.whyCN: 总数并不说明有多少人分享它，因此这个短语常被按人口除开。

senses.title: The expenditure measure
senses.definition: the calculation of output by adding household, business, government and foreign spending
senses.definitionCN: 把家庭、企业、政府与国外的支出相加来核算产出的方法
senses.example: The expenditure side of gross domestic product rose with retail sales.
senses.exampleCN: 国内生产总值的支出法一侧随零售额上升。
senses.why: Everything produced is bought by someone, so spending can be added up to reach the same total from the demand side.
senses.whyCN: 被生产出来的东西总会被某人买走，因此从需求一侧把支出加起来也能得到同一个总数。

senses.title: The income measure
senses.definition: the calculation of output by adding wages, profits, rents and other incomes earned in production
senses.definitionCN: 把工资、利润、租金等在生产中获得的收入相加来核算产出的方法
senses.example: The income measure of gross domestic product lagged behind spending.
senses.exampleCN: 国内生产总值的收入法结果落后于支出法。
senses.why: The value of output is paid out as incomes, so the same total can be reached by adding what people earned.
senses.whyCN: 产出的价值会以收入形式发放出去，因此把人们赚到的相加也能得到同一个总数。

senses.title: The output measure
senses.definition: the calculation of output by adding the value each industry contributes, net of intermediate inputs
senses.definitionCN: 把各行业贡献的增加值（扣除中间投入）相加来核算产出的方法
senses.example: The output measure of gross domestic product counts each stage only once.
senses.exampleCN: 国内生产总值的生产法对每一环节只计一次。
senses.why: Counting the same loaf at mill, bakery and shop would inflate the total, so each stage contributes only its own addition.
senses.whyCN: 把同一个面包在磨坊、面包房与店铺各计一次会吹大总数，因此每一环节只计入它自己增加的那部分。

senses.title: The limits of GDP as a welfare measure
senses.definition: the shortcoming that output says nothing about distribution, unpaid work, health or environmental cost
senses.definitionCN: 产出并不说明分配、无偿劳动、健康或环境代价的缺陷
senses.example: Critics say gross domestic product counts the clean-up after a spill as a gain.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说，国内生产总值把泄漏事故后的清理也算作增益。
senses.why: Because the measure counts market transactions, harm that costs money to repair can appear as growth, which is why the phrase is often invoked to be criticized.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个度量计的是市场交易，需要花钱修复的损害反而会显示为增长，因此这个短语常被拿来作为批评对象。

intro.en: Gross domestic product joins three words: gross, from Old French gros and Late Latin grossus 'thick, coarse'; domestic, from Latin domesticus 'of the house'; and product, from Latin producere 'to lead forth'. The compound term belongs to twentieth-century national accounting. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gross domestic product 由三个词组成：gross 出自古法语 gros 与晚期拉丁 grossus「厚、粗」；domestic 出自拉丁 domesticus「家的」；product 出自拉丁 producere「引出、产出」。这个复合术语属于 20 世纪国民核算。年代均为约数。

items.en: Grossus meant 'thick, coarse, large'. Source uncertain: its own earlier origin is not established, and Old French gros is the immediate route into English.
items.cn: grossus 意为「厚的、粗糙的、大的」。来源不确定：它更早的来历未得到确认，英语是经古法语 gros 借入的。

items.en: Domus meant 'house, household'; the adjective domesticus 'of the house' supplied English domestic.
items.cn: domus 意为「房屋、家户」；形容词 domesticus「家的」提供了英语 domestic。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere 'to lead' gave producere 'to lead forth, to bring out', and so to bring a thing into being.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere「引导」构成 producere「引出、带出」，因而指把某物造出来。

items.en: Gross entered English in the fourteenth century, domestic in the sixteenth, and product in the fifteenth; each had a life of its own before the phrase existed.
items.cn: gross 于 14 世纪进入英语，domestic 于 16 世纪，product 于 15 世纪；在短语出现之前，每个词都有自己的用法。

items.en: The three words were assembled as one term with the national accounts built in the 1930s and 1940s, when governments needed a single figure for total output.
items.cn: 这三个词是在 20 世纪三四十年代建立国民核算时被组合成一个术语的，当时政府需要一个表示总产出的单一数字。

items.en: The phrase is generally dated to that period, and the abbreviation GDP soon displaced the full form in ordinary reporting.
items.cn: 这个短语一般被认为出自那个时期，缩写 GDP 很快在日常报道中取代了全称。

note.en: The first group holds measures that look almost the same but count different things; the second holds broader names for the size of an economy.
note.cn: 第一组是看起来几乎一样、却计不同东西的度量；第二组是经济规模的更宽泛名称。

entries.definition: Counts output by a country's residents wherever they are, so it includes earnings abroad; the domestic measure counts inside the border.
entries.definitionCN: 按一国居民计算产出，不论他们在哪里，因此包含海外收益；domestic 则只计国境之内。

entries.definition: Subtracts the wearing out of machinery from the gross figure, so it is smaller and closer to sustainable output.
entries.definitionCN: 从总量中扣除机器磨损，因此数值更小，也更接近可持续产出。

entries.definition: Adds up sales at every stage, including intermediate goods, so it double-counts what the product measure counts once.
entries.definitionCN: 把每一环节的销售额都相加，包括中间产品，因此会把 product 只计一次的东西重复计算。

entries.definition: The three initials of the same phrase; in ordinary usage it has largely replaced the full form.
entries.definitionCN: 同一短语的三个首字母；在日常使用中已基本取代全称。

entries.definition: The total earned by residents; it approaches the same figure from incomes rather than from output.
entries.definitionCN: 居民获得的总收入；从收入而非产出接近同一个数字。

entries.definition: The economy's total production, stated without the market-value conventions of the accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 经济体的总产量，不含核算中的市值惯例。

entries.definition: A plain term for what an economy produces; it is not tied to a particular accounting standard.
entries.definitionCN: 经济产出物的日常说法；不绑定某一特定核算标准。

entries.definition: The whole framework of accounts, of which gross domestic product is one headline figure.
entries.definitionCN: 整套核算框架，国内生产总值只是其中的一个头条数字。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: three real words with real roots, a real fixed phrase and a real abbreviation, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：三个有真实词根的词、真实的固定短语与真实缩写，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Read the three words as three limits: gross before deductions, domestic inside the border, product what is made.
normal.cn: 把三个词读成三重限定：gross 是扣除之前，domestic 是国境之内，product 是被造出的东西。

normal.en: The abbreviation takes the initials: G, D and P.
normal.cn: 缩写取三个首字母：G、D 与 P。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: gross domestic product per capita, real gross domestic product, the deflator.
normal.cn: 固定说法：人均国内生产总值、实际国内生产总值、平减指数。

normal.en: Real here means constant prices, not 'true'.
normal.cn: 这里的 real 指不变价格，而不是「真实」。

normal.en: The measure was built with the national accounts of the 1930s and 1940s.
normal.cn: 这个度量是随 20 世纪三四十年代的国民核算建立起来的。

abstract.en: Picture one number standing in for a whole country's year of work.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数字代表整个国家一年的劳作。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where a spill clean-up is entered on the gain side.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，把泄漏清理记在增益一栏。

abstract.en: Picture a map with a border drawn through it, and only what happens inside is counted.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图中间画着国界，只计界内发生的事。

examples.en: Gross domestic product grew by two percent after adjusting for prices.
examples.cn: 剔除价格因素后，国内生产总值增长百分之二。

examples.en: The country's gross domestic product per capita remains below the regional average.
examples.cn: 该国人均国内生产总值仍低于地区平均水平。

examples.en: Economists use gross domestic product as a rough proxy for the size of an economy.
examples.cn: 经济学家用国内生产总值粗略代表经济规模。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「gross（总的）+ domestic（国内的）+ product（产出）」——国内全部产出加起来 → 国内生产总值

root: gross 出古法语 gros／晚期拉丁 grossus「厚、粗」，更早来源存疑；domestic 出拉丁 domesticus「家的」，源自 domus「家」；product 出拉丁 producere「引出」= pro-「向前」+ ducere「引导」。三者于 20 世纪国民核算中合为一词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one total: everything produced inside a border is added up, and that total is then read at current prices, at constant prices, per head, through spending, through incomes, through industry value and finally as a measure of welfare it cannot be.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个总数展开：国境之内生产的一切被加总，这个总数再依次被读作现价、不变价、人均、支出法、收入法、行业增加值，最后被读作一个它承担不了的福祉度量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a year's ledger spread on a table, every finished thing in the country folded into one figure.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摊开一年的账本，全国做成的每样东西被折成一个数字。

branches.en: TOTAL AND LIMIT: the same headline figure that sums output also exposes what output cannot say about well-being.
branches.cn: 总数与限度：汇总产出的同一个头条数字，也暴露了产出无法说明福祉的地方。

branches.en: PRICE BASIS: current prices swell with inflation, constant prices isolate quantity.
branches.cn: 价格基准：现价随通胀膨胀，不变价分离出数量。

branches.en: PER HEAD: a total becomes meaningful only when divided among the people who share it.
branches.cn: 人均：总数只有分到分享它的人头上才有意义。

branches.en: SPENDING AND INCOME: the same total can be reached from what buyers spent or what earners received.
branches.cn: 支出与收入：同一个总数可从买方花掉的或挣得者收到的来得到。

branches.en: VALUE ADDED: counting each stage once keeps the total from double-counting the same loaf.
branches.cn: 增加值：每一环节只计一次，避免把同一个面包重复计算。

intro.en: The phrase is three words, each with its own suffix or root, and the pieces also build a large family of English words.
intro.cn: 这个短语由三个词组成，每个词都有自己的词根或后缀，这些成分还构成一大族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin grossus gives gross and grocer; domus gives domestic, domicile and domain; producere gives product, produce, production and productive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 grossus 衍生出 gross 与 grocer；domus 衍生出 domestic、domicile 与 domain；producere 衍生出 product、produce、production 与 productive。

items.structure: gross (adjective from Old French gros, Late Latin grossus)
items.example: Gross means the whole before anything is taken away.
items.exampleCN: gross 指扣除任何东西之前的整体。

items.example: The root supplies the 'at home' image behind domestic.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供 domestic 背后「在家中」的意象。
这个形容词给出英语 domestic。

items.meaning: of one's own country; of the home
items.example: Domestic here fixes the measure inside the border.
items.exampleCN: 这里的 domestic 把度量固定在国境之内。

items.meaning: to lead forth; to bring out
items.example: The verb pictures something being brought into being.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把某物被造出来的过程画了出来。

items.example: The noun names what is made, not what is earned.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被做出的东西，而非被赚到的收入。

items.example: The suffix builds production from produce.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由 produce 构成 production。

items.example: The suffix builds productive from product.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由 product 构成 productive。

definition_zh: 突变；使突变；改变形态；（语言学）发生元音换音
definition_en: to undergo or cause a genetic change, or more generally to change form or character
core_image: 病毒在宿主里复制出新的版本，外壳上的标记一次比一次略有不同
scene: 病毒在宿主里不断复制，每隔几代就出现新的版本。 Viruses mutate quickly enough to escape older vaccines.
sceneCN: 这里 mutate 指「发生遗传突变」（第 1 个义项：遗传物质发生改变）；句意为病毒突变得足够快，能逃过较旧的疫苗。可辨识物件：病毒示意球、宿主细胞、复制箭头、新旧外壳标记。

senses.title: Undergo a genetic change
senses.definition: to undergo a change in genetic material
senses.definitionCN: 遗传物质发生改变
senses.example: Viruses mutate quickly enough to escape older vaccines.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒突变得足够快，能逃过较旧的疫苗。
senses.why: The core sense is intransitive: the material changes itself, and no outside agent is named.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是不及物的：物质自身发生改变，不点明外部施事者。

senses.title: Cause a genetic change
senses.definition: to induce or create a change in genetic material
senses.definitionCN: 诱发或造成遗传物质的改变
senses.example: Researchers mutate one base to test its function.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者使一个碱基突变，以检验其功能。
senses.why: The transitive use adds an experimenter: the change is made on purpose, often one site at a time.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法加上实验者：改变是有意作出的，常常一次一个位点。

senses.title: Change form or appearance
senses.definition: to change in form, often gradually or beyond recognition
senses.definitionCN: 形态发生改变，常为逐渐或面目全非
senses.example: The story mutated with every retelling.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事每复述一次就变一次。
senses.why: The general sense treats form like sequence: small substitutions accumulate until the thing is recognizably different.
senses.whyCN: 一般义把形态当作序列：小的替换累积起来，直到事物明显不同。

senses.title: Change into something else
senses.definition: to develop into a different kind of thing
senses.definitionCN: 发展成另一种事物
senses.example: The protest mutated into a national movement.
senses.exampleCN: 这场抗议演变成全国性运动。
senses.why: With into, the verb names a threshold: what began as one thing now counts as another.
senses.whyCN: 与 into 连用时，这个动词命名一个门槛：起初是一回事，如今算作另一回事。

senses.title: Undergo vowel mutation
senses.definition: in historical linguistics, to change a vowel under the influence of a following sound
senses.definitionCN: 在历史语言学中，指元音在后接音影响下改变
senses.example: Old English mutated the vowel before a high front vowel.
senses.exampleCN: 古英语在高前元音前使元音发生换音。
senses.why: Philology used the verb for sound change before biology borrowed it, and the linguistic sense remains technical.
senses.whyCN: 语文学在生物学借用之前就用这个动词指语音变化，语言学义至今仍是技术性的。

senses.title: Mutate a pathogen deliberately
senses.definition: to alter a pathogen in the laboratory, often to weaken it
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室中改变病原体，常为削弱它
senses.example: Scientists mutate a strain to weaken it for a vaccine.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家使一个毒株突变，以削弱它用于疫苗。
senses.why: This sense is closer to engineering than to accident: the change is directed toward a goal.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项更接近工程而非偶然：改变被导向一个目标。

senses.title: Mutate rapidly or slowly
senses.definition: to change at a particular rate under given conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在特定条件下以某种速率改变
senses.example: These bacteria mutate faster under antibiotic pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这些细菌在抗生素压力下突变得更快。
senses.why: Rate adverbs turn the verb into a measurable process, which is how mutation becomes a parameter.
senses.whyCN: 速率副词把这个动词变成可测量的过程，突变由此成为参数。

senses.title: Transform a plan or idea
senses.definition: to change a plan, idea or institution until it differs greatly from the original
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、观念或制度改变到与原初大不相同
senses.example: The plan mutated beyond recognition after the review.
senses.exampleCN: 计划在评审之后变得面目全非。
senses.why: The figurative use carries a warning: change without a clear limit can destroy the original purpose.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法带有警示：没有明确界限的改变可能毁掉原初目的。

intro.en: Mutate comes from Latin mutare 'to change'; English may have formed it from the past participle mutatus or as a back-formation from mutation, and both routes are hypotheses. It is first recorded in 1818 for general change, long before genetics.
intro.cn: mutate 来自拉丁 mutare「改变」；英语可能由过去分词 mutatus 构成，也可能是从 mutation 逆构，两条路径都属假说。这个词在 1818 年首次记录为一般变化义，远早于遗传学。

items.en: Mutare 'to change' is the source of mutation, mutable and mutate. Its deeper origin is not established beyond Latin, so any pre-Latin root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: mutare「改变」是 mutation、mutable 与 mutate 的来源。它在拉丁语之外的更深来源未得到确证，因此任何拉丁语之前的词根均属重构。

items.en: The past participle mutatus 'changed' supplied the stem behind the English verb pattern in -ate.
items.cn: 过去分词 mutatus「已改变的」提供了英语 -ate 动词模式背后的词干。

items.en: Mutate appeared in English in 1818 meaning 'to change'; the exact sense development is not fully documented, and the relationship to Latin mutatus is a hypothesis.
items.cn: mutate 在 1818 年以「改变」义出现在英语中；义项发展并无完整文献，且它与拉丁 mutatus 的关系属于假说。

items.en: The genetic sense is recorded from 1913 and twentieth-century genetics made 'undergo mutation' the dominant sense, first of organisms and later of viruses and cells.
items.cn: 遗传义从 1913 年起有记录；20 世纪的遗传学使「发生突变」成为主导义，先用于生物体，后用于病毒与细胞。

items.en: Philologists used mutate for vowel change before the biological sense spread, and the sense survives in historical grammar.
items.cn: 在生物学义传播之前，语文学家已用 mutate 指元音变化，这一义在历史语法中存留。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin and sense dates): mutare has no established deeper etymology, and the dates of the biological and linguistic senses are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语之前词源与义项年代）：mutare 没有已确立的更深词源，生物学义与语言学义的年代都只是约数。

note.en: Group one separates mutate from its family and from a near sound-alike; group two separates it from verbs of changing and transforming.
note.cn: 第一组把 mutate 与其词族及一个音近词分开；第二组把它与「改变」「转变」类动词区分。

entries.definition: The change or the process; mutate is the act of undergoing or causing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指改变或过程；mutate 是发生或导致改变的动作。

entries.definition: An organism carrying a change; it names the result rather than the process.
entries.definitionCN: 携带改变的生物体；命名结果而非过程。

entries.definition: Able to change; the adjective describes a possibility, not an event.
entries.definitionCN: 能够改变；形容词描述可能性，而非事件。

entries.definition: From Latin mutus 'silent', not mutare: unable or unwilling to speak. The resemblance is only in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 mutus「沉默的」，并非 mutare：指不能或不愿说话。相似仅在读音。

entries.definition: The broad everyday verb; mutate is narrower and often implies form or sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 宽泛的日常动词；mutate 更窄，常暗示形态或序列。

entries.definition: To make a partial change, often deliberate; mutate can be unintended and can go further.
entries.definitionCN: 作部分改变，常为有意；mutate 可以无意，且程度可能更深。

entries.definition: To change form completely; mutate stresses repeated or gradual change, especially of sequences.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底改变形态；mutate 强调反复或逐渐的改变，尤指序列。

entries.definition: To develop gradually, especially by selection; mutate names the origin of variation, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐发展，尤经选择；mutate 命名变异来源，而非整个过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mutare 'to change' + -ate: to make or become changed.
normal.cn: mutare「改变」+ -ate：使改变或发生改变。

normal.en: The family runs mutate, mutation, mutant and mutable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mutate、mutation、mutant 与 mutable。

normal.en: Viruses mutate; researchers mutate a site; stories mutate in retelling.
normal.cn: 病毒会突变；研究者使位点突变；故事在复述中变形。

normal.en: Mutation is the noun; mutant is the carrier.
normal.cn: mutation 是名词；mutant 是携带者。

normal.en: Linguistic mutate refers to vowel change, an older sense.
normal.cn: 语言学中的 mutate 指元音换音，是更早的义项。

abstract.en: Picture a photocopier that never makes an exact copy.
abstract.cn: 想象一台永远不能完全准确复印的复印机。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour growing a new detail at every retelling.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻每复述一次就长出一个新细节。

abstract.en: Picture a path worn wider by feet until it becomes a road.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被踩得越来越宽、最终变成道路的小径。

examples.en: The virus mutates slowly enough for the vaccine to remain useful.
examples.cn: 这种病毒突变够慢，疫苗仍能发挥作用。

examples.en: The team mutated the binding site to see what changed.
examples.cn: 团队使结合位点突变，观察发生了什么变化。

examples.en: The old ceremony mutated into a street festival.
examples.cn: 这个古老仪式演变成了街头节日。

dict_mnemonic.text: mut（改变）+ ate（动词尾）——使改变 → 突变；名词是 mutation。

root: 拉丁 mutare「改变」← 过去分词 mutatus；mutare 在拉丁语之外的更深来源不确定，相关原始印欧语词根均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a changing copy: genetic change, induced change, changed form, change into another kind, vowel shift, weakened pathogen, measurable rate and a transformed plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一份不断改变的副本展开：遗传改变、诱发改变、形态改变、变成另一类、元音换音、被削弱的病原体、可测速率与变形的计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a virus copying itself, each shell slightly different from the last.
core.cn: 核心意象：病毒不断复制自身，外壳一次比一次略有不同。

branches.en: GENETIC CHANGE AT A RATE: the material changes itself, fast or slow.
branches.cn: 以某速率发生的遗传改变：物质自身改变，可快可慢。

branches.en: INDUCED CHANGE: an experimenter or vaccine maker directs the change.
branches.cn: 诱发改变：实验者或疫苗制作者引导改变。

branches.en: FORM AND THRESHOLD: appearance shifts, and a thing becomes another kind.
branches.cn: 形态与门槛：外观移动，事物成为另一类。

branches.en: VOWEL SHIFT: historical grammar uses the verb for sound change.
branches.cn: 元音换音：历史语法用这个动词指语音变化。

branches.en: BEYOND RECOGNITION: a plan or idea changes until its purpose is lost.
branches.cn: 面目全非：计划或观念改变到失去原初目的。

intro.en: Mutate is a Latin verb whose stem also builds the noun, the carrier and the adjective; prefixes extend the same root to exchange and unchangeability.
intro.cn: mutate 是拉丁动词，其词干还构成名词、携带者与形容词；前缀把同一词根扩展到「交换」与「不可变」。

latinIntro.en: Latin mutare gives mutate, mutation, mutant and mutable; com- builds commutation, in- builds immutable, trans- builds transmutation. All share the changing root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mutare 衍生 mutate、mutation、mutant 与 mutable；com- 构成 commutation，in- 构成 immutable，trans- 构成 transmutation。它们共享「改变」词根。

items.example: The root names the act of changing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名改变的动作。

items.example: The participle supplied the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供了动词词干。

items.example: The suffix forms a verb from the stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀从词干构成动词。

items.example: The old dream was to transmute lead into gold.
items.exampleCN: 古老的梦想是把铅变成金。

latinEntries.structure: muto, mutare, mutavi, mutatum (verb, first conjugation)

definition_zh: 毁林；森林砍伐；森林覆盖的丧失
definition_en: the removal or clearing of forest cover, usually to convert the land to another use
core_image: 推土机沿山坡推进，成片的树倒下后被烧掉，裸露的红土被雨水冲成沟壑
scene: 推土机沿山坡推进，成片的树倒下后被烧掉，裸露的红土在雨季被冲成沟壑。 Bulldozers moved along the slope, felled trees were burned in heaps, and the bare red soil was cut into gullies by the rains: this is deforestation.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「把森林清除掉的过程」（第 1 个义项：森林被砍伐清除）；句意为推土机沿坡推进，伐倒的树被烧掉，裸露红土被雨水冲出沟壑，这就是毁林。

pos.zh: 被清除后的状态或结果
作为环境驱动因素的毁林
历史上为农业而进行的林地清除

senses.title: Clearing forest
senses.definition: the act of cutting or burning forest to remove tree cover
senses.definitionCN: 通过砍伐或焚烧除去森林覆盖的行为
senses.example: Deforestation begins with roads cut into the forest edge.
senses.exampleCN: 毁林从在森林边缘开出道路开始。
senses.why: This is the core act sense: the trees are deliberately removed.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心行为义：树木被有意清除。

senses.title: Loss of forest cover
senses.definition: the process by which a forested area loses its tree cover over time
senses.definitionCN: 林地在时间中失去树木覆盖的过程
senses.example: Satellite images showed deforestation spreading along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星图像显示毁林沿河流蔓延。
senses.why: The act is now viewed as a process measured in area and time.
senses.whyCN: 行为此时被看作以面积和时间衡量的过程。

senses.title: Conversion to other land use
senses.definition: the change of forest land into farmland, pasture, settlement or infrastructure
senses.definitionCN: 把林地改为农田、牧场、居民点或基础设施
senses.example: Much deforestation here is conversion to cattle pasture.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的毁林大多是改为养牛牧场。
senses.why: The word names the loss from the forest's side, while land-use writing names the gain from the new use's side.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从森林一侧命名损失，而土地利用写作从新用途一侧命名获得。

senses.title: Large-scale logging
senses.definition: the removal of timber over large areas, often for export or industry
senses.definitionCN: 在大面积上采伐木材，常为出口或工业原料
senses.example: Selective logging is not the same as deforestation.
senses.exampleCN: 选择性采伐与毁林不是一回事。
senses.why: Logging removes trees; deforestation means the forest cover does not return.
senses.whyCN: 采伐移走树木；毁林意味着森林覆盖不再恢复。

senses.title: Cleared state
senses.definition: the condition of land after its forest has been removed
senses.definitionCN: 森林被除去后土地所处的状态
senses.example: The deforested slope lost its soil within two seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 被毁林的山坡在两个季节内就失去了土壤。
senses.why: The action noun also names the resulting landscape, which is what later restoration must address.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词也命名结果景观，而这正是后来恢复要面对的对象。

senses.title: Tropical deforestation
senses.definition: the clearing of tropical forests, especially for agriculture and ranching
senses.definitionCN: 热带森林的清除，尤因农业与牧业
senses.example: Tropical deforestation accounts for a large share of emissions.
senses.exampleCN: 热带毁林占排放的很大一部分。
senses.why: The general word is attached to its most politically visible setting.
senses.whyCN: 这个总称词被固定在其最受关注的具体场景上。

senses.title: Environmental driver
senses.definition: deforestation considered as a cause of biodiversity loss, erosion and carbon emissions
senses.definitionCN: 把毁林看作生物多样性丧失、侵蚀与碳排放的原因
senses.example: The report links deforestation to both flooding and species decline.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把毁林与洪水及物种减少都联系起来。
senses.why: The word shifts from an event to a causal factor in environmental systems.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从事件转成环境系统中的因果因素。

senses.title: Historical clearance
senses.definition: the clearing of forest in earlier periods, often for farming or fuel
senses.definitionCN: 较早时期为农业或燃料而清除森林
senses.example: Medieval deforestation left only small woods on the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的毁林只在山脊上留下小片树林。
senses.why: The modern word is applied retrospectively to older land-use change.
senses.whyCN: 现代词被追溯用于更早的土地用途改变。

intro.en: Deforestation is a nineteenth-century formation on de- plus forestation. Its rise as a global environmental term belongs to the twentieth century, and the first date is approximate.
intro.cn: 该词为十九世纪由 de- 加 forestation 构成；成为全球环境术语主要在二十世纪，确切首见年代为大致估计。

items.en: The prefix de- means 'away, down, reversing'. Forest comes from Medieval Latin forestis through Old French, and -ation from Latin -atio marks an action or result.
items.cn: 前缀 de- 意为「离开、向下、反转」。forest 经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 forestis，-ation 来自拉丁语 -atio，标记动作或结果。

items.en: Deforestation is recorded in nineteenth-century writing on land use, often in descriptions of clearing for farms or fuel. French déforestation may have reinforced the form.
items.cn: deforestation 见于十九世纪有关土地利用的写作，常描述为农田或燃料而进行的清除。法语 déforestation 可能强化了这一形式。

items.en: The term became global with tropical forest loss after the mid-twentieth century, when satellites made the loss visible as area and rate.
items.cn: 二十世纪中期以后，随着热带森林丧失，这个词走向全球；卫星让损失以面积与速度变得可见。

items.en: Climate and biodiversity policy made deforestation a driver to be measured, reported and regulated, including through zero-deforestation supply chains.
items.cn: 气候与生物多样性政策把毁林变成需要测量、报告与监管的驱动因素，包括零毁林供应链。

items.en: The word now covers deliberate clearing, agricultural conversion and the resulting loss of cover, and is often used retrospectively for earlier centuries.
items.cn: 这个词现在涵盖有意清除、农业转换以及由此造成的覆盖丧失，也常被追溯用于更早的世纪。

note.en: The first group is close in form but names a different act or a different scale; the second group shares the removal or loss meaning without being interchangeable.
note.cn: 第一组在形式上接近，但命名不同行为或不同尺度；第二组共享清除或丧失的意思，但不能互换。

entries.definition: the establishment of forest cover; it is the reverse of deforestation, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 造林。建立森林覆盖，是毁林的相反过程，不是同义词。

entries.definition: planting forest on land without recent forest; it is a kind of forestation, not a kind of deforestation.
entries.definitionCN: 新造林。在近期无林地上造林，是造林的一种，不是毁林的一种。

entries.definition: a change of shape, from forma 'form'; it has no forest element.
entries.definitionCN: 变形。来自 forma「形状」，不含森林成分。

entries.definition: the general removal of trees or obstacles from land; it can be small-scale and need not mean permanent forest loss.
entries.definitionCN: 清除；清理。从土地上移除树木或障碍，可小规模，也不必然意味着永久失去森林。

entries.definition: the cutting and transporting of timber; it may leave the forest able to regenerate, unlike deforestation.
entries.definitionCN: 伐木。砍伐与运输木材，森林可能仍能更新，不像毁林那样。

entries.definition: the removal of vegetation to prepare land for another use; it is the purpose-neutral description of the same act.
entries.definitionCN: 土地清理。为准备其他用途而清除植被，是对同一行为的用途中立描述。

entries.definition: the net loss of forest area or quality; it includes degradation as well as complete clearing.
entries.definitionCN: 森林丧失。森林面积或质量的净损失，包括退化与完全清除。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is de- 'away' plus forestation, so it literally means the undoing of forest creation.
normal.cn: 这个词是 de-「去除」加 forestation，字面就是「取消造林的结果」。

normal.en: The family runs deforest, deforested, deforestation-free and reforestation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 deforest、deforested、deforestation-free 与 reforestation。

normal.en: Collocations: tropical deforestation, deforestation rate, deforestation driver.
normal.cn: 搭配：热带毁林、毁林速度、毁林驱动因素。

normal.en: Logging removes trees, but deforestation means the cover does not return.
normal.cn: 伐木移走树木，但毁林意味着覆盖不再恢复。

normal.en: Zero-deforestation supply chains are a policy instrument of the 2010s.
normal.cn: 零毁林供应链是二十一世纪一十年代的政策工具。

abstract.en: Picture a road pushed into intact forest, with bare ground widening behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路推进完整森林，后面裸地不断变宽。

abstract.en: Picture a satellite image where a green block turns brown year by year.
abstract.cn: 想象卫星图上一块绿色逐年变褐。

abstract.en: Picture smoke from burned felled trees rising over a hillside of stumps.
abstract.cn: 想象被烧的伐倒木冒烟，下方是布满树桩的山坡。

examples.en: Deforestation in the basin reduced dry-season water storage.
examples.cn: 流域内的毁林减少了旱季的蓄水量。

examples.en: The company pledged to remove deforestation from its supply chain.
examples.cn: 该公司承诺从供应链中消除毁林。

examples.en: Historical deforestation left the ridge with thin, eroded soils.
examples.cn: 历史上的林地清除让山脊只剩薄而受侵蚀的土壤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「去掉 + 森林」——把森林覆盖从土地上拿掉 → 毁林

root: 由 de-「去除」加 forestation 构成，十九世纪见于土地利用写作；forest 经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 forestis。作为全球环境术语主要在二十世纪流行，确切首见年代为大致估计。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the act of clearing to the process of loss, the land-use conversion, the logging that may or may not cause it, the resulting landscape, the tropical setting, the environmental causal role and retrospective historical clearance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从清除行为，到丧失过程、土地用途转换、可能造成也可能不造成毁林的采伐、结果景观、热带场景、环境因果角色，再到追溯性的历史林地清除。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green block being cut back to bare soil, year after year.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块绿色被逐年削回裸土。

branches.en: ACT AND PROCESS: deliberate clearing and the measured loss it produces.
branches.cn: 行为与过程：有意清除，以及它造成的可测丧失。

branches.en: CONVERSION AND LOGGING: one changes the use, the other removes timber; only the first is necessarily deforestation.
branches.cn: 转换与采伐：前者改变用途，后者移走木材；只有前者必然是毁林。

branches.en: THE BARE RESULT: land left without its cover.
branches.cn: 裸露的结果：失去覆盖后的土地。

branches.en: TROPICS AND DRIVERS: the most visible setting and the causal role in climate and biodiversity.
branches.cn: 热带与驱动：最显眼的场景，以及在气候与生物多样性中的因果角色。

branches.en: RETROSPECT: the modern word applied to old land-use change.
branches.cn: 回溯：现代词用于旧的土地用途改变。

intro.en: Deforestation is a transparent English formation whose parts come from Latin and French; the affix section separates the reversing prefix from the forest base and the action suffix.
intro.cn: deforestation 是透明的英语构造，各成分来自拉丁语与法语；词缀部分把反转前缀与森林基础词、动作后缀分开。

latinIntro.en: Latin de- supplies the reversing prefix, Medieval Latin forestis supplies the base, and Latin -atio supplies the action suffix. The French form may have reinforced the English one.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 de- 提供反转前缀，中世纪拉丁语 forestis 提供基础，拉丁语 -atio 提供动作后缀。法语形式可能强化了英语形式。

items.example: The company was fined for deforesting the reserve.
items.exampleCN: 该公司因清除保护区森林被罚款。
被毁林的山坡迅速侵蚀。

items.example: The label marks a deforestation-free product.
items.exampleCN: 这个标签标记零毁林产品。
被清除的地带随后进行了造林。

items.example: The forest once covered the whole basin.

items.meaning: net loss of forest area or quality
removal of vegetation for another use
items.example: Land clearing is the purpose-neutral description.
items.exampleCN: 土地清理是用途中立的描述。

definition_zh: 联邦制；联邦主义；中央与地方分权的原则；（组织内部的）分权体制
definition_en: a system of government in which power is divided between a central authority and constituent units, or the principle or movement that advocates such a division
core_image: 一张地图被两种颜色的铅笔画过，同一条河的上游与下游各有自己的税则，中央只在交界处盖章
scene: 十几个代表围着一张大地图，用两种颜色标出中央与各州各自可以征税的范围。 On the map the delegates drew two colours to show what federalism left to each level of government.
sceneCN: 这里 federalism 指中央与地方分权的政府体制（第 1 个义项：联邦制的权力划分）；句意为代表们用两种颜色在大地图上标出联邦制留给中央与各州各自的权限。图中可辨识物件：大地图、双色铅笔、州界线、盖章处。

pos.zh: 联邦制；联邦主义；分权原则；（组织内的）分权安排

forms.label: 复数（指多种联邦制安排）

derivatives.zh: 联邦主义者 / 联邦主义的
使结成联邦；使归联邦管辖
邦联主义（各单位保留更大主权）

senses.title: Power split between centre and units
senses.titleCN: 中央与成员单位分权的政府体制
senses.definition: a system in which a central government and regional governments each hold powers that the other cannot simply take away
senses.definitionCN: 一种中央政府对地区政府各自握有对方不能随意剥夺的权力的制度
senses.example: On the map the delegates drew two colours to show what federalism left to each level of government.
senses.exampleCN: 代表们用两种颜色在大地图上标出联邦制留给中央与各州各自的权限。
senses.why: The word is built on foedus 'treaty': units that once stood apart bind themselves by an agreement that each side keeps, so power is shared by contract rather than granted from above.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 foedus「盟约」之上：原本分立的单位以一份各方都保留的约定结合，因此权力是按契约共享，而非由上而下授予。

senses.title: The principle, not the machine
senses.titleCN: 作为政治原则的联邦主义
senses.definition: the doctrine that governing power should be divided among levels rather than concentrated in one
senses.definitionCN: 主张治理权力应在多个层级间划分、而非集中于一处的主张
senses.example: Her essay defended federalism as a check on any single capital.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文章把联邦主义辩护为对任何单一权力中心的制约。
senses.why: A working arrangement can also be argued for as a value, and in that shift the noun stops describing an institution and starts describing a belief.
senses.whyCN: 一套运作安排也可以被当作价值来论证；在这一转手里，名词不再描述制度，而开始描述信念。

senses.title: A movement seeking union
senses.titleCN: 谋求结成联邦的政治运动
senses.definition: a movement that works to bring separate states or nations into a single federal union
senses.definitionCN: 致力于把分立的国家或民族结合为一个联邦联盟的运动
senses.example: Post-war federalism pushed for a directly elected European assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 战后的联邦主义推动了直选欧洲议会的出现。
senses.why: If a treaty can bind units, then someone will want to extend the treaty to new units, and the noun becomes the name of that campaign.
senses.whyCN: 既然盟约能约束各单位，就会有人想把盟约扩展到新的单位，名词于是成为那场运动的名字。

senses.title: The early American party line
senses.titleCN: 美国早期联邦党人主张的用法（专名义）
senses.definition: the programme of the late eighteenth-century American party that wanted a stronger central government
senses.definitionCN: 十八世纪末美国那个主张强化中央政府的政党所持的纲领
senses.example: Textbooks use federalism for the programme that funded a national bank and a standing fleet.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书用联邦主义指那套为国家银行与常备舰队提供资金的纲领。
senses.why: A party took the adjective as its name, and its programme inherited the noun, so one capitalised use points to a specific historical camp.
senses.whyCN: 一个政党把这个形容词当作党名，其纲领便继承了名词，因此有一个大写用法指向特定的历史阵营。

senses.title: Power sharing inside an organisation
senses.definition: the division of authority between a central body and regional branches of a union, party or church
senses.definitionCN: 工会、政党或教会中中央机构与地区分支之间的权限划分
senses.example: The union's federalism gave each branch the right to set its own strike ballot.
senses.exampleCN: 这个工会的联邦制让每个分支都有权自行决定是否投票罢工。
senses.why: The pattern of divided authority is easy to copy into any large body, so the noun travels from states to offices without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 分权的模式很容易被复制到任何大型组织，于是这个名词从国家移到办公室而形状不变。

senses.title: Fiscal federalism
senses.titleCN: 财政职能在各级政府间的划分
senses.definition: the arrangement by which taxing and spending duties are allocated among levels of government
senses.definitionCN: 税收与支出职责在各级政府之间分配的制度安排
senses.example: Economists study fiscal federalism to see which level should pay for schools.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家研究财政联邦主义，以判断应由哪一级政府为学校出资。
senses.why: Money follows the same line as law: if each level keeps its own revenue, it can act without asking the centre for every sum.
senses.whyCN: 钱跟着同一条线走：每一级保留自己的收入，就能不经中央逐笔拨款而行动。

senses.title: A doctrine of limited central power
senses.titleCN: 宪法解释中限制中央权力的主张
senses.definition: a reading of a constitution that reserves broad powers to the states and reads central powers narrowly
senses.definitionCN: 一种把广泛权力保留给各州、对中央权力作狭窄解释的宪法读法
senses.example: The court's federalism argument blocked the federal agency from regulating local water.
senses.exampleCN: 法院依联邦主义的主张，禁止联邦机构监管地方水域。
senses.why: If the split is written into a constitution, judges must decide where the line falls, and the noun becomes an argument about how to read that line.
senses.whyCN: 既然分权写进了宪法，法官就必须判定界线在哪里，名词于是变成一场关于如何读这条线的论证。

senses.title: A design choice in comparative politics
senses.titleCN: 比较政治中的一种制度设计选择
senses.definition: one of the institutional models a divided or multi-ethnic state may adopt, alongside unitary and confederal arrangements
senses.definitionCN: 分裂社会或多民族国家可选的一种制度模型，与单一制和邦联制并列
senses.example: Comparing federalism with unitary rule shows how many veto points each design creates.
senses.exampleCN: 把联邦制与单一制相比，可以看出每种设计产生多少个否决点。
senses.why: Once the arrangement is treated as a choice rather than a fact, the noun can be listed beside rival designs and weighed by their effects.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这套安排被当作可选而非既定，名词就能与竞争设计并列，并按效果被衡量。

intro.en: Federalism is federal plus -ism; federal goes back through French to Latin foedus 'treaty, league'. The political noun was coined in the late eighteenth century, when American writers needed a name for divided sovereignty.
intro.cn: federalism 由 federal 加表示学说的后缀构成；federal 经法语上溯到拉丁 foedus「盟约、同盟」。这个政治名词在十八世纪后期被造出，当时美国作者需要一个名字来称呼被分割的主权。

items.en: Foedus, genitive foederis, meant a treaty, league or covenant. The word names the bond itself, which is why federal arrangements are described as contractual rather than hierarchical.
items.cn: foedus（属格 foederis）意为盟约、同盟、约定。这个词命名的是纽带本身，因此联邦安排被描述为契约式而非层级式。

items.en: It is generally thought that foedus shares a root with fides 'faith, trust', from a reconstructed element meaning 'to trust'; the shared root is a reasoned reconstruction, not a recorded form.
items.cn: 一般认为 foedus 与 fides「信义、信任」共享一个词根，该词根出自一个表示「信任」的重构成分；这一共享词根属有理据的重构，并非有记录的词形。

items.en: French fédéral and the earlier Latin-derived foederalis carried the sense 'of a league' into early modern usage, still close to treaty and alliance.
items.cn: 法语 fédéral 以及更早由拉丁派生的 foederalis 把「同盟的」这一义带入近代早期用法，仍贴近盟约与结盟。

items.en: Federalism appears in English political writing in the seventeen-eighties and nineties, naming the division of sovereignty between a national government and the states.
items.cn: federalism 在十八世纪八九十年代的英语政治写作中出现，指国家政府与各州之间对主权的划分。

items.en: American writers also used it, often capitalised, for the programme of the party that favoured a stronger centre, which is how one proper-noun sense arose.
items.cn: 美国作者也用它（常大写）指那个偏向强化中央的政党的纲领，专名的一义即由此而来。

items.en: The earliest citation is not precisely dated: the seventeen-eighties figure is approximate, and earlier isolated uses in translation remain unverified.
items.cn: 最早书证没有精确年代：十八世纪八十年代只是约数；更早散见于译本中的用例尚未得到证实。

note.en: The first group is built on the same treaty word and is often mixed up; the second group names other ways of distributing authority.
note.cn: 第一组同出那个表示盟约的词，常被混淆；第二组是其他分配权力的方式。

entries.definition: The adjective describing anything belonging to a union of states, or to the central level of one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述属于州联合体的事物，或属于其中央层级的事物。

entries.definition: The union itself as an entity, such as a national federation of clubs; federalism is the principle behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 指联合体这个实体，如全国性俱乐部联合会；联邦主义是其背后的原则。

entries.definition: A supporter of the arrangement, or the adjective describing such a position.
entries.definitionCN: 指这种安排的支持者，或描述该立场的形容词。

entries.definition: A looser union in which the units keep most sovereignty and the centre depends on their consent.
entries.definitionCN: 更松散的联合，各单位保留大部分主权，中央依赖它们的同意。

entries.definition: The Latin noun for treaty or league; it is the source of the whole English group.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示盟约或同盟的名词，是整个英语词组的来源。

entries.definition: The handing of specified powers from a central parliament to regional bodies that remain subordinate.
entries.definitionCN: 中央议会把特定权力交给仍处于从属地位的地区机构。

entries.definition: Moving offices and decisions away from a capital without giving regions constitutional protection.
entries.definitionCN: 把机构与决策从首都外移，但不给地区宪法层面的保障。

entries.definition: A state in which one parliament holds final authority and regions act only as its agents.
entries.definitionCN: 由一个议会掌握最终权威、地区仅作为其代理人的国家。

entries.definition: The right of a group to govern its own affairs within limits set elsewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 在外部设定的限度内自行管理事务的权利。

entries.definition: The doctrine that decisions should be made in one place and applied uniformly.
entries.definitionCN: 主张决策应在一处作出并统一施行的主张。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin treaty word, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「盟约」词、真实的同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Foedus is Latin for treaty, so federalism is government by a kept agreement.
normal.cn: foedus 是拉丁语「盟约」，所以联邦制就是靠一份被各方共同遵守的约定来治理。

normal.en: The family runs federal, federalism, federalist, federalise, federalisation and federation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 federal、federalism、federalist、federalise、federalisation 与 federation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical senses: fiscal federalism, dual federalism, cooperative federalism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：财政联邦主义、二元联邦主义、合作联邦主义。

normal.en: The same root gives fides, faith or trust, which is why a treaty and a pledge sound alike in Latin.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 fides「信义」，所以在拉丁语里盟约与誓言听起来相近。

normal.en: One capital letter changes the reference: Federalism with a capital names a historical party line.
normal.cn: 一个大写字母就换了所指：大写的联邦主义指历史上的一个党派纲领。

abstract.en: Picture a map inked in two colours, neither able to erase the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被两种颜色画过的地图，哪一种都擦不掉另一种。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge whose planks are owned by the villages at either end, not by the river.
abstract.cn: 想象一座绳桥，桥板归两端村子所有，而不归河流所有。

abstract.en: Picture two keys to one door, cut differently, so neither side can open it alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门有两把齿形不同的钥匙，任何一方都无法独自打开。

examples.en: The constitution's federalism is visible in its list of state powers.
examples.cn: 宪法中的联邦制体现在它所列的州权清单上。

examples.en: Fiscal federalism explains why schools depend on local taxes.
examples.cn: 财政联邦主义解释了学校为何依赖地方税收。

examples.en: Supporters argued that federalism protects minorities from distant majorities.
examples.cn: 支持者认为联邦制能保护少数群体不受远方多数的支配。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「federal（联邦的）+ ism（主义）」——主张中央与地方分权的制度 → 联邦制

root: 拉丁 foedus（属格 foederis）「盟约、同盟」，一般认为与 fides「信义」共享一个表示「信任」的重构词根 → 法语 fédéral → 英语 federal → federalism。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line drawn on a map: the line divides power, becomes a principle, then a campaign, then a party programme, then a rule inside a union, a budget rule, a judicial reading, and finally a model on a shelf of designs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕地图上画的一条线：这条线分割权力，随后成为原则、运动、党派纲领、工会内部的章程、预算规则、司法读法，最后成为设计清单上的一种模型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one line on a map, drawn by two hands, that neither side may rub out.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一条由两只手共同画的线，任何一方都擦不掉。

branches.en: STRUCTURE AND MODEL: a working arrangement and a design choice are the same line seen in a country or on a shelf.
branches.cn: 制度与模型：运作中的安排与清单上的设计，是同一条线出现在一个国家或一个架子上。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: once the line is defended as a value, the noun stops describing and starts advocating.
branches.cn: 论证：一旦这条线被当作价值来辩护，名词就不再描述，而开始主张。

branches.en: TWO CAMPAIGNS: a movement extending the treaty outward, and a party defending a stronger centre inward.
branches.cn: 两场运动：一场向外扩展盟约，一场向内维护更强的中央。

branches.en: THE OFFICE COPY: states are replaced by branches, and the same line is drawn inside a union.
branches.cn: 办公室的复本：国家换成分支，同一条线被画在工会内部。

branches.en: MONEY AND LAW: budgets and judicial readings are the line turned into arithmetic and into interpretation.
branches.cn: 钱与法：预算与司法读法，是这条线变成算术与解释的两副面孔。

intro.en: Federalism rests on a Latin treaty noun that also builds federal, federation and confederation, plus a doctrine suffix.
intro.cn: 联邦主义依赖一个拉丁语「盟约」名词，它同时构成 federal、federation 与 confederation，末尾再加表示学说的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin foedus, genitive foederis, gives foederalis and through French federal; the same root is behind fides 'faith'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 foedus（属格 foederis）给出 foederalis，再经法语成为 federal；同一词根还在 fides「信义」背后。

items.example: The root names the bond, not the ruler.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名纽带，而非统治者。

items.example: It turns the treaty noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把盟约名词变成形容词。

items.example: The adjective describes the union and its centre.
items.exampleCN: 形容词描述联合体及其中央。

items.example: It names the principle as a whole.
items.exampleCN: 它把原则作为整体来命名。

items.example: The noun can mean the machine or the belief.
items.exampleCN: 名词既可指机器，也可指信念。

items.meaningCN: 联邦主义者；联邦主义的
items.example: One form serves person and adjective.
items.exampleCN: 一个词形兼指人与形容词。

items.example: It forms the verb of conversion.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示转变的动词。

items.example: The verb names the act of drawing the line.
items.exampleCN: 动词命名画这条线的动作。

items.example: It marks the looser union in confederation.
items.exampleCN: 它在「邦联」中标出更松的结合。

definition_zh: 香气；芳香；（比喻）韵味、气息
definition_en: a pleasant noticeable smell, especially from food or drink
core_image: 咖啡壶里飘出的暖香
scene: 清晨的厨房里，水汽正从壶嘴袅袅升起。 The aroma of fresh coffee filled the room.
sceneCN: 这里 aroma 是「香气」（第 1 个义项：怡人的气味）；句意是新煮咖啡的香气弥漫房间。

collocations.phrase: the aroma of the old world

senses.title: A pleasant smell from food or drink
senses.definition: a strong, pleasant smell, especially one given off by cooking, coffee or wine
senses.definitionCN: 浓郁怡人的气味，尤指烹饪、咖啡或葡萄酒散发的香味
senses.example: The aroma of baking bread drifted down the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 烤面包的香气飘下楼梯。
senses.why: The Greek word first meant spice, the very source of pleasant smells.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原词本指「香料」，正是怡人气味的源头。

senses.title: A distinctive pervading quality
senses.definition: a noticeable quality or atmosphere surrounding a person, place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 环绕人、地、物的可感知特质或气氛
senses.example: The old hotel keeps the aroma of a vanished era.
senses.exampleCN: 这家老饭店保留着逝去时代的韵味。
senses.why: A smell spreads through air, so the word extends to immaterial atmospheres.
senses.whyCN: 气味在空气中弥散，词义便延伸到无形的氛围。

intro.en: Aroma comes from Greek arōma, meaning spice or sweet herb.
intro.cn: aroma 源自希腊语 arōma，本义「香料、香草」。

items.en: The root is uncertain; some link it to words for fragrant substances.
items.cn: 词根不确定，一般认为与表示芳香物质的词相关（来源不确定）。

items.en: Arōma meant spice, sweet herb, and also an aromatic balm for the body.
items.cn: 希腊语 arōma 指香料、香草，也指涂身的芳香油膏。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as aroma with the same spice sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该词作 aroma，仍指香料。

items.en: English took aroma from Latin in the seventeenth century for fragrant plants and drugs.
items.cn: 17 世纪英语经拉丁语借入 aroma，指芳香植物与药材。

items.en: The smell sense shifted from plants to food, and then to figurative atmospheres.
items.cn: 气味义由植物转向食物，进而衍生出比喻的氛围义。

note.en: Aroma is pleasant by definition; odor and smell stay neutral or worse.
note.cn: aroma 天然偏褒义；odor 与 smell 中性或偏负。

entries.definition: having a pleasant smell; in chemistry, of benzene-like compounds
entries.definitionCN: 芳香的；（化学）芳香族的，aroma 的同根形容词

entries.definition: treatment using aromatic plant oils
entries.definitionCN: 用芳香植物油进行的芳香疗法，aroma 的同根复合词

entries.definition: a mistake
entries.definitionCN: 错误，只是拼写相近，与香气义毫无关系

entries.definition: a sweet or pleasant smell
entries.definitionCN: 甜美的气味，与 aroma 同为褒义气味词

entries.definition: a smell, natural or artificial, pleasant or not
entries.definitionCN: 气味，涵盖天然与人造、好闻与难闻，语域比 aroma 宽

entries.definition: a pleasant smell, or scented liquid
entries.definitionCN: 芳香的气味或香水，侧重人工调制的香

normalIntro.en: Keep the food connection and the -atic adjective in mind.
normalIntro.cn: 记住与食物的关联及 -atic 形容词形式。

normal.en: aroma = a good smell, almost always of food or drink.
normal.cn: aroma 指好闻的气味，几乎总与食物饮品相关。

normal.en: The adjective is aromatic: aromatic herbs.
normal.cn: 形容词是 aromatic：芳香草本。

normal.en: In chemistry, aromatic compounds are benzene-based.
normal.cn: 化学中 aromatic compounds 指苯环化合物。

normal.en: Common phrase: the aroma of fresh coffee.
normal.cn: 常见搭配：新煮咖啡的香气。

normal.en: Figuratively, the aroma of success means its atmosphere.
normal.cn: 比喻用法：成功的气息。

abstract.en: Picture steam curling up from a morning cup under a window light.
abstract.cn: 想象晨光里杯中袅袅升起的水汽。

abstract.en: Recall the smell of garlic hitting hot olive oil.
abstract.cn: 回忆蒜香撞入热橄榄油的气味。

abstract.en: See the scent as a soft golden cloud spreading through a room.
abstract.cn: 把香味想成一团金色软云漫过房间。

examples.en: The kitchen was filled with the aroma of cinnamon rolls.
examples.cn: 厨房里满是肉桂卷的香气。

examples.en: Wine tasters praise its full-bodied aroma.
examples.cn: 品酒师称赞它浓郁的芳香。

examples.en: The market has the aroma of a hundred cuisines.
examples.cn: 这集市弥漫着百般菜系的韵味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿肉妈」——阿妈炖肉，香气飘满整条街，邻居循味来敲门，这就是「阿肉妈」的香气。

root: 希腊语 arōma（香料、香草）→ 拉丁语 aroma → 英语 aroma；同根形容词 aromatic（芳香的；芳香族的）。

sensesIntro.en: From spice and pleasant smell to the immaterial flavor of a place or time.
sensesIntro.cn: 由香料与怡人气味延伸到地方或时代无形的韵味。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: warm scent drifting invisibly through the air
core.cn: 核心意象：暖香无形地在空气中飘散

branches.en: smell that stirs appetite
branches.cn: 勾起食欲的气味

branches.en: spice as the original source
branches.cn: 作为本源的香料

branches.en: scent tied to memory
branches.cn: 与记忆相连的气息

branches.en: atmosphere as spread-out smell
branches.cn: 如弥散香气的氛围

branches.en: a character all its own
branches.cn: 独一无二的特质

intro.en: Aroma heads a small smell family completed by the adjective aromatic.
intro.cn: aroma 领衔一个小小的气味词族，形容词 aromatic 补齐全貌。

latinIntro.en: Latin kept the Greek word unchanged when borrowing it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借入该希腊词时几乎未作改动。

definition_zh: 形成概念；概念化；把…抽象为观念；构思；用概念解释；概念化设计
definition_en: to form a concept or idea of something; to interpret an experience in terms of concepts; to plan something in the mind
core_image: 一团模糊的雾被几根线框住，慢慢显出轮廓，可以被指着说“这是X”
scene: 设计师先把用户的需求从「想要更快」抽象成「减少等待的步骤」。 Designers first conceptualize the user's need, turning 'I want it faster' into 'fewer steps to wait through', and only then draw the screen.
sceneCN: 这里 conceptualize 是「概念化、把某事物抽象成概念」（第 2 个义项：用概念来理解和表述经验）；句意：设计师先把用户需求概念化，把「想要更快」变成「减少等待的步骤」，然后才画界面。图中可辨识物件：模糊雾团、线框、便利贴、需求清单、界面草图。

pos.zh: 形成概念；概念化；构思；用概念解释

senses.title: Form a concept
senses.definition: to build a general idea from particular cases
senses.definitionCN: 从具体案例建立一般观念
senses.example: Children conceptualize animals before they name them.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童在命名之前就先形成动物概念。
senses.why: This is the core sense: particulars are compressed into a category. The verb describes a cognitive achievement, and it can be gradual, partial, or failed.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义：具体被压缩成范畴。该动词描述认知成就，可以渐进、部分或失败。

senses.title: Interpret through concepts
senses.definition: to understand an experience by placing it under concepts
senses.definitionCN: 把经验放到概念之下以理解
senses.example: The study conceptualizes poverty as a lack of capability.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究把贫困概念化为能力不足。
senses.why: Academic usage makes the verb programmatic: a phenomenon is framed in a particular vocabulary. The framing is an argument, because another vocabulary would make other facts visible.
senses.whyCN: 学术用法使该动词纲领化：现象被特定词汇框定。框定即论证，因为另一套词汇会让另一些事实显现。

senses.title: Plan in the mind
senses.definition: to work out the main idea of something before making it
senses.definitionCN: 在制作前想清某物的主要想法
senses.example: They conceptualized the app before writing code.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在写代码前先构思了这款应用。
senses.why: Design and engineering use the verb for the front end of a project. Nothing exists yet, but the relations that will govern the artifact are already being fixed.
senses.whyCN: 设计与工程用该动词指项目前端。尚无实物，但将支配成品的关系已被固定。

senses.title: Conceptual design
senses.definition: to define a design at the level of purpose and structure
senses.definitionCN: 在目的与结构层面界定设计
senses.example: The team conceptualized the building as a stack of courts.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把这座建筑概念化为层层叠起的庭院。
senses.why: Architecture uses the verb for the governing metaphor of a project. A strong conceptualization gives every later decision a reason; a weak one leaves decisions arbitrary.
senses.whyCN: 建筑用该动词指项目的统摄隐喻。强的概念化给此后每个决定以理由；弱的则使决定任意。

senses.title: Explain by concepts
senses.definition: to make something intelligible by assigning it to known categories
senses.definitionCN: 通过把某物归入已知范畴而使其可理解
senses.example: We conceptualize grief as a process, not an event.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把悲伤概念化为过程，而非事件。
senses.why: This is the explanatory use: categorization does work. Calling grief a process changes what one expects, measures, and offers, so the concept is practical as well as descriptive.
senses.whyCN: 这是解释性用法：归类在做工。把悲伤称为过程，改变人们期待、测量与提供之物，故概念既描述又实践。

senses.title: Conceptualize others
senses.definition: to form a mental model of another person's mind or role
senses.definitionCN: 对他人心智或角色形成心理模型
senses.example: The child begins to conceptualize others as having beliefs.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童开始把他人概念化为拥有信念的存在。
senses.why: Developmental psychology uses the verb for theory of mind: another person becomes an object with hidden states. The word marks a step from behaviour to inference.
senses.whyCN: 发展心理学用该动词指心理理论：他人成为有隐藏状态的对象。该词标记从行为到推论的步骤。

senses.title: Classify as a concept
senses.definition: to treat something as an instance of a category
senses.definitionCN: 把某物当作某范畴的实例
senses.example: The report conceptualizes the protests as a single movement.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把抗议概念化为单一运动。
senses.why: This sense is close to classification but adds a claim: the category is treated as real enough to organize events. The act can be contested, since the grouping may be imposed rather than found.
senses.whyCN: 此义近于分类，但多一个主张：该范畴被当作足以组织事件的实在。此动作可被质疑，因为分组可能是强加的，而非发现的。

senses.title: Build a conceptual model
senses.definition: to construct a simplified model of entities and relations
senses.definitionCN: 建构实体与关系的简化模型
senses.example: The researchers conceptualized the system as a network.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者把该系统概念化为网络。
senses.why: Modelling uses the verb for choosing the ontology of a study. Before measuring, one decides what counts as an entity and what as a relation; that decision is the conceptualization.
senses.whyCN: 建模用该动词指选择研究的本体。测量之前先决定什么算实体、什么算关系；该决定就是概念化。

senses.title: Conceptual art practice
senses.definition: to make the idea itself the work, or to treat materials as carriers of ideas
senses.definitionCN: 使观念本身成为作品，或把材料当作观念载体
senses.example: The artist conceptualized the gallery as a waiting room.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术家把画廊概念化为候诊室。
senses.why: Contemporary art uses the verb for the move that turns a situation into an idea. The object may remain, but its role is to point at the concept rather than to be the concept.
senses.whyCN: 当代艺术用该动词指把情境转为观念的动作。实物可以仍在，但其角色是指向观念，而非成为观念。

intro.en: Conceptualize is conceptual plus -ize, an English formation of the 19C. Conceptual is concept plus -ual, from Latin conceptus, from concipere 'take in, conceive' (com- plus capere 'take'). The -ize suffix goes back through Latin -izare to Greek -izein, used to form verbs meaning 'make or treat as'. So conceptualize is literally 'to make conceptual'. British spelling conceptualise follows the same suffix.
intro.cn: conceptualize 是 conceptual 加 -ize，是十九世纪的英语构造。conceptual 是 concept 加 -ual，出自拉丁 conceptus，源于 concipere“摄入、构想”（com- 加 capere“拿”）。-ize 后缀经拉丁 -izare 上溯希腊 -izein，用于构成“使…、把…当作”的动词。故 conceptualize 字面即“使概念化”。英式拼写 conceptualise 用同一后缀。

items.en: conceptus, from concipere 'take in', is the noun base; conceptual adds -ualis 'relating to'.
items.cn: conceptus 出自 concipere“摄入”，是名词词基；conceptual 加 -ualis“与…有关”。

items.en: The suffix -izein forms verbs of making or treating as; Latin -izare and French -iser carry it onward.
items.cn: 后缀 -izein 构成“使…、把…当作”的动词；拉丁 -izare 与法语 -iser 将其传下。

items.en: English -ize is productive from the 16C; conceptualize is a learned 19C coinage on the adjective.
items.cn: 英语 -ize 自十六世纪起能产；conceptualize 是十九世纪在形容词上的学术新造词。

items.en: Philosophy and psychology adopt conceptualize for the act of forming or applying concepts.
items.cn: 十九世纪哲学与心理学采用 conceptualize 指形成或应用概念的动作。

items.en: Design, education, and cognitive science extend it to planning, teaching, and model building.
items.cn: 二十世纪设计、教育与认知科学把它扩展到规划、教学与建模。

items.en: British conceptualise and American conceptualize are the same verb with different spelling conventions.
items.cn: 英式 conceptualise 与美式 conceptualize 是同一动词的不同拼写惯例。

note.en: The first group is the conceptual family and its spelling variants; the second is verbs of thinking, which differ in whether they form an idea, plan it, or merely understand it.
note.cn: 第一组是 conceptual 词族及拼写变体；第二组是思维动词，差别在于形成观念、规划还是仅仅理解。

entries.definition: relating to concepts.
entries.definitionCN: 与概念有关的。

entries.definition: the act or result of forming a concept.
entries.definitionCN: 形成概念的动作或结果。

entries.definition: British spelling of conceptualize.
entries.definitionCN: conceptualize 的英式拼写。

entries.definition: to express an idea in a precise, often formal, form. It stresses wording more than category-making.
entries.definitionCN: 以精确、常正式的形式表达想法。更强调措辞，而非造范畴。

entries.definition: to set up a problem or issue within a particular perspective. It is close to sense 02 but more rhetorical.
entries.definitionCN: 在特定视角内设置问题。近第 2 义，但更修辞。

entries.definition: to form a mental picture. It is more sensory and less categorical than conceptualize.
entries.definitionCN: 形成心理图像。比 conceptualize 更感官、更少范畴性。

normalIntro.en: Real links: conceptual plus the -ize suffix 'make/treat as', the capere root, and the British/American spelling split.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：conceptual 加表“使…/当作”的 -ize 后缀、capere 词根，以及英美拼写分歧。

normal.en: Conceptual + -ize = 'make conceptual'. The suffix turns an adjective into a verb of making.
normal.cn: conceptual + -ize =“使概念化”。该后缀把形容词变成“使…”动词。

normal.en: -ize goes back to Greek -izein through Latin -izare; it is the same suffix as in modernize and organize.
normal.cn: -ize 经拉丁 -izare 上溯希腊 -izein；与 modernize、organize 是同一后缀。

normal.en: Concept is from capere 'take'; conceptualize is the mind taking a case and holding it under a category.
normal.cn: concept 出自 capere“拿”；conceptualize 是心智拿起一个案例，把它放到范畴之下。

normal.en: British conceptualise, American conceptualize: same verb, spelling convention only.
normal.cn: 英式 conceptualise、美式 conceptualize：同一动词，只是拼写惯例。

normal.en: To conceptualize grief as a process changes what you expect and offer; the concept does work.
normal.cn: 把悲伤概念化为过程，会改变你期待与提供之物；概念在做工。

abstract.en: Conceptualizing is choosing a vocabulary, and every vocabulary makes some facts visible while hiding others.
abstract.cn: 概念化就是选择词汇，而每套词汇让一些事实显现，同时遮住另一些。

abstract.en: To conceptualize is to compress the particular into the general, and something is always lost in the compression.
abstract.cn: 概念化是把个别压缩为一般，而压缩中总有东西丢失。

abstract.en: A model's ontology is its politics: what counts as an entity decides who or what can appear in the analysis.
abstract.cn: 模型的本体就是其政治：什么算实体，决定谁或什么能出现在分析中。

examples.en: It is hard to conceptualize a universe without time.
examples.cn: 很难概念化一个没有时间的宇宙。

examples.en: The team conceptualized the problem as a flow of resources.
examples.cn: 团队把问题概念化为资源流动。

examples.en: Children conceptualize the world through stories and play.
examples.cn: 儿童通过故事与游戏概念化世界。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of conceptualize: form a concept, interpret through concepts, plan in the mind, define a design idea, explain by categories, model another mind, classify as a concept, build a model, and make the idea the artwork.
sensesIntro.cn: conceptualize 的九个义项：形成概念、用概念理解、心中构思、界定设计理念、用范畴解释、建模他人心智、归为概念、建立模型、使观念成为艺术。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY: forming a concept and treating a case as an instance are the basic moves.
branches.cn: 范畴：形成概念与把案例当作实例是基本动作。

branches.en: THE EXPLANATION: a vocabulary frames a phenomenon and changes what counts as a fact.
branches.cn: 解释：词汇框定现象，改变什么算事实。

branches.en: THE PLAN: design and architecture fix the governing idea before making anything.
branches.cn: 计划：设计与建筑在制作前固定统摄理念。

branches.en: THE MIND: another person becomes a model with hidden states.
branches.cn: 心智：他人成为有隐藏状态的模型。

branches.en: THE MODEL AND THE ART: an ontology or an artwork makes the idea the object.
branches.cn: 模型与艺术：本体或艺术品使观念成为对象。

intro.en: Conceptualize is conceptual + -ize. Conceptual is concept + -ual, from Latin conceptus. The -ize suffix comes through Latin -izare from Greek -izein. The family includes conceptualization, conceptual, concept, and conception; the British spelling is conceptualise.
intro.cn: conceptualize 是 conceptual 加 -ize。conceptual 是 concept 加 -ual，出自拉丁 conceptus。-ize 后缀经拉丁 -izare 来自希腊 -izein。词族含 conceptualization、conceptual、concept、conception；英式拼写为 conceptualise。

latinIntro.en: Latin conceptus 'a conception' plus -ualis gives conceptualis. English adds -ize to the adjective, a suffix of Greek origin meaning 'make or treat as'. The noun conceptualization adds -ation. The same base yields concept and conception.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 conceptus“构想”加 -ualis 给出 conceptualis。英语在形容词上加 -ize，这是源自希腊、意为“使…/把…当作”的后缀。名词 conceptualization 加 -ation。同一词基给出 concept 与 conception。

dict_mnemonic.text: dissentious ＝ dissent（持异议；dis-「分开」＋ sentire「感受、认为」）＋ -ious（充满…的）＝「满是不同意见的」，指人爱争、指事惹争；同根还有 consent（一致同意）、sentiment（情感）。

definition_zh: 银行账户；客户在银行开立、用于存放资金并记录收支的户头
definition_en: an arrangement with a bank that holds a customer's money and records payments, withdrawals and interest
core_image: 一只写着名字的抽屉，钱进钱出都在抽屉旁的小本上留下痕迹
scene: 开学前，新生在分行填好表格，把生活费交给柜台。 Every student needs a bank account before the scholarship arrives.
sceneCN: 这里 bank account 指「在银行开立的存款户头」（第 1 个义项：银行代为保管资金的账户安排）；句意为每个学生在奖学金到账前都需要一个银行账户。图中可辨识物件：开户表格、存折、柜台、缴费通知单。

senses.title: The arrangement with a bank
senses.titleCN: 与银行订立的账户安排
senses.definition: an agreement under which a bank keeps a customer's money and records every movement of it
senses.definitionCN: 银行保管客户资金并记录其每一笔变动的约定
senses.example: Every student needs a bank account before the scholarship arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学生在奖学金到账前都需要一个银行账户。
senses.why: bank names the institution and account names the reckoning it keeps for one customer, so the phrase is the record plus the promise to keep it.
senses.whyCN: bank 指机构，account 指它为某个客户保存的结算，因此这个短语是记录加上保存记录的承诺。

senses.title: The money on deposit
senses.definition: the balance actually held in such an arrangement at a given moment
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻该安排中实际存放的余额
senses.example: The bank account holds barely enough for the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 这个银行账户里的钱几乎只够付房租。
senses.why: people name the container for what it contains, so the account came to mean the money inside it.
senses.whyCN: 人们常用容器指代其中的内容，于是账户也指其中的钱。

senses.title: A product type
senses.definition: one of the standard products a bank sells, such as a savings or a current account
senses.definitionCN: 银行出售的标准产品之一，如储蓄账户或活期账户
senses.example: A savings account pays a little interest each month.
senses.exampleCN: 储蓄账户每月支付少量利息。
senses.why: once banks offered several designs, the phrase began to name each product rather than any one arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 当银行提供多种设计后，这个短语开始指每一种产品，而不只是某一项安排。

senses.title: The identifying number
senses.definition: the number or code that identifies one such arrangement in a payment system
senses.definitionCN: 在支付系统中标识某项账户安排的号码或代码
senses.example: Write the bank account on the transfer form.
senses.exampleCN: 把银行账号写在转账单上。
senses.why: in a network each account must be findable, so the word is used for its address as well as for the thing addressed.
senses.whyCN: 在网络中每个账户都必须能被找到，于是这个词既指账户本身，也指它的地址。

senses.title: A shared account
senses.definition: an account held jointly by two or more people who can all draw on it
senses.definitionCN: 由两人或多人共同持有、各自都可支取的账户
senses.example: The couple keeps a joint bank account for rent.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妇为付房租保留了一个联名银行账户。
senses.why: the arrangement can be held by more than one person, and joint ownership is named by prefixing the phrase rather than by changing it.
senses.whyCN: 这种安排可以由不止一人持有，共有关系通过在短语前加修饰词表示，而不改变短语本身。

senses.title: An earmarked account
senses.definition: an account opened by an organization or a person to keep one purpose's money separate
senses.definitionCN: 组织或个人为把某一用途的资金分开保存而开立的账户
senses.example: The charity opened a separate bank account for donations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构为捐款单独开了一个银行账户。
senses.why: separating money by purpose is the accounting habit that gave each column its own account, applied inside a bank.
senses.whyCN: 按用途分钱是会计的老习惯，让每一栏各有一个账目，这一习惯被搬进了银行。

senses.title: A digital account record
senses.definition: the online view of the arrangement, where balances and transactions appear as data
senses.definitionCN: 该安排在网络上的视图，余额与交易以数据形式呈现
senses.example: Her bank account was frozen while the bank checked the transfer.
senses.exampleCN: 银行核查这笔转账期间，她的银行账户被冻结了。
senses.why: the same record now lives in software, but the phrase stayed with the record rather than with the ledger.
senses.whyCN: 同一份记录如今存于软件之中，但短语仍跟着记录走，而不是跟着账簿走。

senses.title: A reserve of trust, figuratively
senses.definition: a store of goodwill or credibility that a person can draw on later
senses.definitionCN: 一个人日后可以动用的善意或信誉储备
senses.example: Goodwill is a bank account you draw on in hard times.
senses.exampleCN: 善意是一个在艰难时能取用的银行账户。
senses.why: the metaphor treat trust as money: it can be deposited by good acts and withdrawn when help is needed.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把信任当作金钱：善举是存入，需要帮助时是支取。

intro.en: Bank account pairs the moneychanger's bench with a Latin reckoning. The two words met in English banking in the eighteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: bank account 把「钱商柜台」与一个拉丁「结算」词并置。两个词在 18 世纪的英格兰银行业相遇。年代均为约数。

items.en: Bank came into English through French and Italian from banca, the bench where a moneychanger counted coins.
items.cn: bank 经法语与意大利语进入英语，源自 banca，即钱商数钱的柜台。

items.en: Account descends from computare 'to reckon together', built on com- and putare, and reached English through Old French acont.
items.cn: account 来自 computare「合起来计算」，由 com- 与 putare 构成，经古法语 acont 进入英语。

items.en: As London banks kept a separate ledger page for each customer, the page was called the customer's account, and the phrase bank account followed.
items.cn: 当伦敦的银行替每位客户保存单独的账簿页时，这一页被称为客户的 account，bank account 这一短语随之出现。

items.en: Savings banks in the nineteenth century turned the account into a product, and cheque clearing gave it a number.
items.cn: 19 世纪的储蓄银行把账户变成一种产品，支票清算又给了它一个号码。

items.en: From the later twentieth century the account has been a database record, though the older ledger vocabulary survives in statements and passbooks.
items.cn: 从 20 世纪后期起，账户成为数据库中的记录，但旧账簿词汇仍留在对账单与存折上。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the first use of the exact phrase is not fixed, and both banca and putare rest on reconstructed earlier forms.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这一确切短语的最早用例没有定论，banca 与 putare 的早期形式都属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms that look close because they share the stem account; group two holds documents and figures that sit beside a real bank account.
note.cn: 第一组是因共用 account 词干而形近的形式；第二组是与真实银行账户配套出现的单据与数字。

entries.definition: The single word can mean any account, including a story or an explanation; the compound narrows it to a bank.
entries.definitionCN: 单词本身可指任何账目，包括叙述或解释；复合短语把它收窄到银行。

entries.definition: The person who keeps and checks accounts, not the record itself.
entries.definitionCN: 保存与核查账目的人，不是记录本身。

entries.definition: The profession of keeping accounts, which looks close but names work rather than a record.
entries.definitionCN: 保存账目的职业，字形相近但指工作而非记录。

entries.definition: A periodic list a bank sends, showing what moved in the account; it is not the account itself.
entries.definitionCN: 银行定期寄出的清单，列出账户内的资金变动；它不是账户本身。

entries.definition: The amount standing in the account at one moment, as opposed to the arrangement that holds it.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻账户中的金额，与持有它的安排相对。

entries.definition: A type of account that pays interest and restricts withdrawals, a narrower label than bank account.
entries.definitionCN: 付息并限制支取的账户类型，是比 bank account 更窄的标签。

entries.definition: The account used for daily payments, called a checking account in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 用于日常支付的账户，美式英语称 checking account。

entries.definition: A locked box in a vault for valuables; it resembles an account in function but holds objects.
entries.definitionCN: 金库中存放贵重物品的锁箱；功能上与账户相似，但存的是物件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bank comes from the moneychanger's bench; account comes from a Latin verb of reckoning.
normal.cn: bank 来自钱商柜台；account 来自一个拉丁「计算」动词。

normal.en: The family runs bank, account, accountant, accounting, accountancy and banking.
normal.cn: 同族包括 bank、account、accountant、accounting、accountancy 与 banking。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: open a bank account, a joint bank account, a frozen bank account.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：开立银行账户、联名银行账户、被冻结的银行账户。

normal.en: The same record is called an account in Britain and often a bank account in full on forms.
normal.cn: 同一份记录在英国简称 account，在表格上常写全为 bank account。

normal.en: A statement reports the account; it is not the account.
normal.cn: 对账单是报告账户情况，它本身不是账户。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer with a name on it and a small notebook lying open beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只写着名字的抽屉，旁边摊开一本小本子。

abstract.en: Picture a jar of trust that fills with each favour and empties when help is asked.
abstract.cn: 想象一只信任的罐子，每次帮忙就装满一点，求助时就倒出一些。

abstract.en: Picture one page in a huge book, kept for you alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一本巨书中单独为你保存的一页。

examples.en: The branch opened her bank account in twenty minutes.
examples.cn: 分行在二十分钟内为她开好了银行账户。

examples.en: A joint bank account lets either partner pay the bills.
examples.cn: 联名银行账户让伴侣任何一方都能付账。

examples.en: He emptied the bank account before the trip.
examples.cn: 出发前他取空了银行账户里的钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「银行 + 账户」——银行替你记账的那一页 → 银行账户

root: 意大利 banca「钱商柜台」（中世纪拉丁 bancus）+ 拉丁 computare「合起来计算」（com- + putare）；两个成分经法语进入英语，18 世纪在银行业合成这一短语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one record: a bank keeps a page for a customer, and that page is then named for the money on it, the product it belongs to, its number, its shared or earmarked form, its digital image and finally a store of trust.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一份记录展开：银行替客户保存一页，这一页再依次指其中的钱、所属的产品、它的号码、共有或专用的形式、数字映像，最后指一种信任储备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one named page in a bank's ledger, with money entering and leaving beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：银行账簿中写着名字的一页，钱在它旁边进出。

branches.en: THE PROMISE: the bank undertakes to keep the money and keep the page.
branches.cn: 承诺：银行承担保管资金与保存这一页的责任。

branches.en: THE CONTENT: the money inside the record, whether seen in a passbook or on a screen.
branches.cn: 内容：记录中的钱，无论看在存折上还是屏幕上。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: banks sell several standard designs, and each one gets the name.
branches.cn: 产品：银行出售几种标准设计，每一种都得到这个名称。

branches.en: THE ADDRESS AND THE SHARERS: a number finds it, and a joint name shares it.
branches.cn: 地址与共有人：号码找到它，联名共享它。

branches.en: SETTING MONEY APART: earmarking a purpose and storing goodwill are the same gesture outside banking.
branches.cn: 把钱分开：为用途专款专用与储存善意，是银行之外的同一种动作。

intro.en: This compound joins a Germanic bench-word turned bank to a Latin reckoning; neither half is a prefix or suffix, so the reading is two free forms plus their endings.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把一个由日耳曼「长凳」词变成的 bank 接在一个拉丁「结算」词上；两半都不是前缀或后缀，因此读法是两个自由词形加各自的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin computare and putare underlie account, count and discount; Medieval Latin bancus supplies bank.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 computare 与 putare 构成 account、count 与 discount 的基础；中世纪拉丁 bancus 提供 bank。

items.exampleCN: 这家银行占用街角的建筑。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着结算的动作。

会计是一门受监管的职业。

items.example: The branch manager is accountable for the loss.
items.exampleCN: 分行经理须为这笔损失负责。
