items.example: The bank offered a discount on fees.
items.exampleCN: 银行在手续费上给了折扣。

definition_zh: 顶点；最高潮；最终成果；达到顶峰的阶段
definition_en: the highest or climactic point that a process reaches, or the act of reaching it
core_image: 登山队在最后一段雪坡上排成一列，把旗子插上峰顶
scene: 登山队在最后一段雪坡上排成一列，把旗子插上峰顶。 The summit was the culmination of ten years of planning.
sceneCN: 这里指长期努力达到的最高点（第 1 个义项：顶点、最高潮）；句意为登顶是十年筹划的顶点。图中可辨识物件：雪坡、冰镐、旗子、峰顶。

pos.zh: 名词：顶点；最高潮；最终成果（可数，常用单数）

collocations.phrase: the culmination of years of work

derivatives.zh: 同一词根的动词，义为「达到顶点；以……告终」
由该动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「达到顶点的」
由该词根加形容词词尾构成，义为「处于最高点的」
同一拉丁词根的直接借用，义为「山顶；最高点」

senses.title: The highest point of a long effort
senses.definition: the point at which a long process reaches its highest level
senses.definitionCN: 一个长期过程达到最高水平的时刻
senses.example: The summit was the culmination of ten years of planning.
senses.exampleCN: 登顶是十年筹划的顶点。
senses.why: The Latin noun for a mountain top gave the word its shape: a process climbs and ends at a peak.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示山顶的名词给了它形状：一个过程向上爬，最后停在峰顶。

senses.title: The final result of a process
senses.definition: the finished outcome in which earlier stages are gathered up
senses.definitionCN: 把先前各阶段收拢在一起的最终结果
senses.example: The treaty was the culmination of months of quiet talks.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约是数月低调谈判的最终成果。
senses.why: A peak gathers everything below it, so the last stage stands for the whole effort.
senses.whyCN: 峰顶把下方的一切都收拢起来，因此最后一阶段代表全部努力。

senses.title: The peak of a career
senses.definition: the most successful or honoured moment of a working life
senses.definitionCN: 职业生活中最成功或最受尊崇的时刻
senses.example: The award marked the culmination of her career.
senses.exampleCN: 这个奖项标志着她职业生涯的顶峰。
senses.why: A working life rises and then levels off, and the word marks the moment it stands highest.
senses.whyCN: 职业生涯会上升然后走平，这个词标记它站在最高处的那一刻。

senses.title: The climax of a ceremony
senses.definition: the most solemn or exciting moment of a formal event
senses.definitionCN: 正式活动中最庄严或最激动人心的时刻
senses.example: The lighting of the flame was the culmination of the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 点燃圣火是典礼的高潮。
senses.why: A ceremony is built as a slope, and the word names the step everyone waits for.
senses.whyCN: 典礼像一段斜坡，这个词点出所有人都在等的那一步。

senses.title: The peak of a trend, including a bad one
senses.definition: the point at which a development reaches its extreme before turning
senses.definitionCN: 某种发展在转向之前达到极端的时刻
senses.example: The crisis was the culmination of months of tension.
senses.exampleCN: 这场危机是数月紧张局势的顶点。
senses.why: A peak can be a summit or a breaking point; the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 顶点可以是登顶，也可以是崩断点，这个词两者都管。

senses.title: Astronomical culmination
senses.definition: the moment a celestial body reaches its highest point above the horizon
senses.definitionCN: 天体到达地平线以上最高点的时刻
senses.example: The star's culmination occurs shortly after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗星的最高点出现在午夜过后不久。
senses.why: Astronomy kept the literal meaning: the body is literally at the top of its arc.
senses.whyCN: 天文学保留了字面义：天体确实处在其弧线的最高处。

senses.title: The climax of a story or artwork
senses.titleCN: 故事或艺术作品的顶点
senses.definition: the most intense point of a narrative or composition
senses.definitionCN: 叙事或作品中最强烈的时刻
senses.example: The final movement is the culmination of the whole symphony.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一个乐章是整部交响曲的顶点。
senses.why: A composition gathers its themes into one last passage, and that passage is the peak the word names.
senses.whyCN: 作品把各个主题收进最后一段，那一段就是这个词所指的高点。

senses.title: The finale of a season or competition
senses.titleCN: 赛季或赛事的收官高潮
senses.definition: the last and highest event that closes a series of contests
senses.definitionCN: 结束一系列赛事的最后一场高潮
senses.example: The final match was the culmination of a long season.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛是整个漫长赛季的收官高潮。
senses.why: A series needs an ending that outranks every earlier round, and the word supplies that ranking.
senses.whyCN: 一连串赛事需要一个压过此前各轮的分量收尾，这个词提供这种排序。

intro.en: Culmination comes from Late Latin culminatio, from culminare, to reach the top, from culmen, a summit or roof. English took the noun in the seventeenth century, first for astronomy and then for human affairs.
intro.cn: 这个词来自晚期拉丁语 culminatio，源头是动词 culminare「到达顶端」，后者出自名词 culmen「山顶、屋顶」。英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，先用于天文，后用于人事。

items.en: The noun meant a summit, a roof or the top of anything.
items.cn: 这个名词意为山顶、屋顶或任何东西的顶端。

items.en: The verb meant to raise to the top or to reach the summit.
items.cn: 这个动词意为抬到顶端或到达峰顶。

items.en: The noun named the act of reaching the highest point.
items.cn: 这个名词指到达最高点的行为。

items.en: English used the word first in astronomy, for a star's highest point.
items.cn: 英语最初在天文中使用这个词，指一颗星的最高点。

items.en: Later usage applied it to careers, ceremonies and finished works.
items.cn: 后来的用法把它用于职业、典礼与完成的作品。

items.en: Modern usage also calls a crisis the culmination of a trend; the date of that extension is uncertain.
items.cn: 现代用法也把危机称为某种趋势的顶点；这一扩展的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the top-of-arc image; the second group names neighbouring high points.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根或「弧线最高点」的意象；第二组是相邻的高点概念。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to reach the highest point or end in something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为达到顶点或以某结果告终。

entries.definition: The participle used as an adjective for a peak stage.
entries.definitionCN: 分词作形容词，指达到顶点的。

entries.definition: An adjective for something at its highest point.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指处于最高点的。

entries.definition: A borrowed Latin noun for a summit.
entries.definitionCN: 借自拉丁语的名词，指山顶。

entries.definition: A pillar, from a related word for a tall upright mass.
entries.definitionCN: 指柱子，出自一个表示高耸竖直物的相关词。

entries.definition: The most intense moment of a narrative or event, stressing intensity rather than height.
entries.definitionCN: 指叙事或事件最强烈的时刻，强调强度而非高度。

entries.definition: The highest level or value reached, often in graphs.
entries.definitionCN: 指达到的最高水平或数值，常用于曲线。

entries.definition: The top of a mountain, and by extension a meeting of leaders.
entries.definitionCN: 指山峰顶端，引申为领导人会议。

entries.definition: The point directly above an observer, used figuratively for a high point.
entries.definitionCN: 指观测者正上方的点，喻指高峰。

entries.definition: The act of finishing rather than the highest point.
entries.definitionCN: 指完成的行为，而非最高点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the literal image of a mountain top, then follow the word into careers, ceremonies and stories.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用山顶的字面意象，再把这个词走到职业、典礼与故事里。

normal.en: The Latin noun meant the top of a mountain, so culmination is the moment a long climb ends.
normal.cn: 拉丁名词意为山顶，所以这个词就是漫长攀登结束的那一刻。

normal.en: The treaty ending months of talks is the finished result, not merely the last event.
normal.cn: 结束数月谈判的条约是最终成果，而不只是最后一场活动。

normal.en: An award can mark the culmination of a career, the highest point of a working life.
normal.cn: 奖项可以标志职业生涯的顶点，即职业生涯的最高处。

normal.en: Astronomy uses the word literally for a star at the top of its arc.
normal.cn: 天文学用它的字面义，指处在弧线最高处的星。

normal.en: A crisis can be the culmination of tension, because a peak may also be a breaking point.
normal.cn: 危机可以是紧张局势的顶点，因为顶点也可能是崩断点。

abstract.en: A peak is the smallest possible place from which everything below can be seen.
abstract.cn: 峰顶是最小的位置，却能从那里看见下方的一切。

abstract.en: Not every culmination is happy: some are simply the last point before a fall.
abstract.cn: 并非每个顶点都令人欣喜：有些只是坠落前的最后一点。

abstract.en: The word gathers time into a single height, which is why we remember summits and forget slopes.
abstract.cn: 这个词把时间收进一个高度，所以我们记住峰顶，忘了斜坡。

examples.en: The exhibition was the culmination of five years of research.
examples.cn: 这场展览是五年研究的顶点。

examples.en: His retirement speech was the culmination of a long career.
examples.cn: 他的退休演说是一段漫长职业生涯的顶点。

examples.en: The festival's culmination came with the final procession.
examples.cn: 节庆的顶点出现在最后的游行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「卡尔米内申」——一路往上爬，最后站到最高的那一点，就是「顶点、高潮」：顶点、最高潮

root: 来自晚期拉丁语 culminatio，源头动词 culminare「到达顶端」，后者出自 culmen「山顶、屋顶」；英语在十七世纪借入，先用于天文，后用于人事。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one shape, a process rising to its top: an effort, a result, a career, a ceremony, a trend, a star, a work and a season.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项保持同一个形状，即过程升到顶端：努力、成果、职业、典礼、趋势、星体、作品与赛季。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a climbing team roped on the last snow slope, a flag planted on the summit.
core.cn: 核心意象：最后一段雪坡上结组而行的登山队，以及插上峰顶的旗。

branches.en: THE HIGHEST POINT: a long effort or a working life reaches its peak.
branches.cn: 最高点：长期努力或职业生涯达到顶峰。

branches.en: THE FINAL RESULT: the treaty and the final match gather the stages below them.
branches.cn: 最终成果：条约与决赛把下面的各阶段收拢起来。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC CLIMAX: a ceremony and a work of art reach their most intense moment.
branches.cn: 公开的高潮：典礼与艺术作品达到最强烈的时刻。

branches.en: THE PEAK OF A TREND: tension can culminate in a crisis.
branches.cn: 趋势的顶点：紧张局势可以以危机告终。

branches.en: THE LITERAL ARC: a star stands at the top of its path across the sky.
branches.cn: 字面的弧线：星体处在它横过天空的路径最高处。

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin noun for a summit, so its parts describe a top and the act of reaching it.
intro.cn: 这个词建在表示山顶的拉丁名词上，各部件描述一个顶端与到达它的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the noun for a summit, the verb of reaching it and the Late Latin noun of the act.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示山顶的名词、表示到达的动词，以及晚期拉丁语中表示该行为的名词。

items.example: The noun gives the word its height.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词给这个词高度。

items.example: The verb describes the climb's last step.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述攀登的最后一步。

items.example: The noun supplied the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供了英语词。

items.example: English formed the verb from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 英语由同一词干构成动词。

items.example: It forms the adjective for a peak stage.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示顶点阶段的形容词。

items.example: It forms the noun of the act.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示行为的名称。

items.example: The noun now covers careers and stories.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词如今也管职业与故事。

items.example: It forms a rare adjective for the highest.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示最高点的少见形容词。

items.example: The verb culminate is followed by in.
items.exampleCN: 动词之后常接介词表示结果。

definition_zh: 求爱；追求；求偶期；（动物）求偶行为
definition_en: the period and the behavior through which one person or animal tries to win the affection and consent of another
core_image: 雄孔雀把巨大的尾屏完全展开，绕雌鸟缓慢转身，每一个姿势都停同样一拍
scene: 雄孔雀把尾屏完全展开，绕雌鸟缓慢转身，每个姿势都保持同样一拍。 The male peacock fans his tail and turns slowly around the female, holding each position for the same beat: a courtship that follows a fixed script.
sceneCN: 这里 courtship 指「为赢得对方好感而进行的一整套展示行为」（第 3 个义项：动物求偶行为）；句意为雄孔雀按固定节奏展开尾屏、绕雌鸟转身，这正是求偶。可辨识物件：展开的尾屏、雌鸟、草地、固定停留的姿势。

pos.zh: （动物行为学）求偶行为；求偶展示

forms.label: 复数（多段追求期；多种求偶行为）
相关名词（宫廷；球场；追求）

derivatives.zh: 有礼的（同出 court，语义已偏）

senses.title: The act of wooing a person
senses.titleCN: 追求某人、争取其好感的行为
senses.definition: the attention and effort one person gives another in order to win affection
senses.definitionCN: 一个人为赢得另一人好感而付出的关注与努力
senses.example: Their courtship lasted two years before the engagement.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的追求持续了两年才订婚。
senses.why: The word began as the behaviour of a courtier, someone who attends a court, and the polite attention of that role became the model for winning favour.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指朝臣的举止，即在宫廷中侍奉的人所表现的那种礼数，而这份周到的关注后来成了赢得欢心的范本。

senses.title: The period before a union
senses.definition: the stretch of time during which two people develop a romantic relationship
senses.definitionCN: 两个人发展恋爱关系所经历的一段时间
senses.example: The novel describes a long rural courtship of letters and walks.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说描写了一段由书信与散步构成的漫长乡间追求期。
senses.why: Because wooing takes time, the noun came to name the time itself, not only the acts within it.
senses.whyCN: 因为追求需要时间，这个名词便开始命名那段时间，而不只是其中的动作。

senses.title: Animal courtship behavior
senses.definition: the displays and signals by which an animal solicits a mate
senses.definitionCN: 动物为招引配偶而进行的展示与信号
senses.example: The dance is courtship, and the female chooses on the basis of it.
senses.exampleCN: 这场舞就是求偶，雌性据此做出选择。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the human word for the same sequence of approach, display and acceptance, because the shape of the behaviour is recognisably alike.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了这个人类词，用来指同样由接近、展示与接受构成的序列，因为行为形状明显相似。

senses.title: A fixed sequence of displays
senses.definition: a stereotyped order of movements performed in a set order before mating
senses.definitionCN: 交配前按固定顺序进行的一套刻板动作
senses.example: The courtship has eleven steps, and a missed step ends it.
senses.exampleCN: 这套求偶有十一个步骤，漏掉一步就结束。
senses.why: Once courtship is a signal, it can be scripted, and a script that must be followed exactly is what makes the display readable to a partner.
senses.whyCN: 一旦求偶成为信号，它就可以被写成脚本；而必须严格遵循的脚本，正是让展示对配偶可读的原因。

senses.title: Gifts and feeding as courtship
senses.titleCN: 以礼物或喂食作为求偶
senses.definition: the offering of food or objects as part of wooing
senses.definitionCN: 把食物或物件作为追求的一部分献上
senses.example: In some species courtship means a gift of prey.
senses.exampleCN: 在某些物种里，求偶意味着一份猎物作礼物。
senses.why: A gift is a display that costs the giver something, and cost is exactly what makes it evidence of serious intent.
senses.whyCN: 礼物是让给出者付出代价的展示，而代价正是使它成为认真意图之证据的东西。

senses.title: The art of paying court
senses.definition: attentive behaviour aimed at winning the favour of someone powerful
senses.definitionCN: 为赢得有权者青睐而表现出的殷勤举止
senses.example: His courtship of the committee was tireless and transparent.
senses.exampleCN: 他对委员会的争取不知疲倦，也毫不掩饰。
senses.why: The courtier's original task was to gain favour, and that older political sense survives whenever someone courts a body rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 朝臣原本的任务就是争取恩宠，只要有人追求的是一个机构而非一个人，这个更早的政治义就会复活。

senses.title: A campaign to win support
senses.definition: a sustained effort to attract voters, clients or allies
senses.definitionCN: 为吸引选民、客户或盟友而进行的持续努力
senses.example: The party's courtship of rural voters began early.
senses.exampleCN: 该党对乡村选民的争取很早就开始了。
senses.why: Political language borrows the whole arc of wooing, from first approach to promised union, and applies it to blocs of supporters.
senses.whyCN: 政治语言借用了求爱的整条弧线，从初次接近到许诺结合，并把它用于支持者群体。

senses.title: Abstract: the art of winning over
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：赢得人心的技艺
senses.definition: any deliberate effort to turn indifference into acceptance
senses.definitionCN: 任何把冷淡转为接纳的有意努力
senses.example: The book is a courtship of the reader, patient and unhurried.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是对读者的一次追求，耐心而不催促。
senses.why: At its widest the word describes a strategy of approach rather than a relationship, and that is why it can be applied to readers or ideas.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个词描述一种接近的策略，而非一段关系，因此它能用于读者或观念。

intro.en: Courtship is court plus the native suffix -ship. Court comes through Old French from Latin cohors 'enclosed yard, company of attendants', and -ship from Old English -scipe 'state or condition of being'.
intro.cn: courtship 是 court 加本族后缀 -ship。court 经古法语来自拉丁 cohors「围起的院子、随从队伍」，-ship 来自古英语 -scipe「处于某种状态」。

items.en: Cohors meant 'enclosed yard, enclosure', and also 'a company of soldiers or attendants'. The link to hortus 'garden' is generally accepted, both going back to a root meaning 'to enclose'.
items.cn: cohors 意为「围起的院子、围场」，也指「一队士兵或随从」。它与 hortus「花园」的联系一般被接受，两者都可追溯到意为「围住」的词根。

items.en: Old French cort 'king's court, princely residence' entered English in the late twelfth century, bringing both the place and the assembled company.
items.cn: 古法语 cort「国王的宫廷、君主居所」在 12 世纪晚期进入英语，同时带来地点与聚集的人群两层意思。

items.en: Old English -scipe formed abstract nouns of state or condition, as in friendship and lordship; it gives courtship the sense of a role or a period.
items.cn: 古英语 -scipe 构成表示状态或身份的名词，如 friendship 与 lordship；它使 courtship 带有「角色或时期」的意思。

items.en: Courtship is recorded from the 1570s meaning 'the behaviour of a courtier, the arts of a court'.
items.cn: courtship 自 16 世纪 70 年代有记录，义为「朝臣的举止、宫廷的技艺」。

items.en: By the 1590s the word named the attention paid to win someone's affection, and by the 1830s it named the whole period of a developing romance.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪 90 年代，这个词指为赢得某人好感而付出的关注；到 19 世纪 30 年代，它指整段发展中的恋情。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date of the animal sense): the biological use of courtship is twentieth-century usage, and no single earliest citation is agreed, so it should be treated as approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（动物义的首见年代）：courtship 的生物学用法属 20 世纪，最早书证没有统一说法，因此应视为约数。

note.en: Group one separates words from the same court stock that now mean different things; group two holds nouns for neighbouring stages of the same approach.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出 court 词干、今义不同的词；第二组是同一接近过程中相邻阶段的名词。

entries.definition: The source noun: a royal court, a playing area, or the verb 'to woo'; courtship is the abstract noun of that verb.
entries.definitionCN: 来源名词：宫廷、球场，或动词「追求」；courtship 是该动词的抽象名词。

entries.definition: From the manners expected at court: it means polite, with no reference to wooing.
entries.definitionCN: 来自宫廷应有的礼数：意为有礼，与求爱无关。

entries.definition: A person who attends a royal court; the original courtship was this person's behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 出入宫廷的人；最初的 courtship 正是这种人的举止。

entries.definition: Polite behaviour as a social code; it shares the court root but not the romantic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 作为社交规范的礼貌举止；共用 court 词根，但无恋爱义。

entries.definition: The activity of trying to win someone's love; it stresses effort, while courtship can also name the period.
entries.definitionCN: 争取某人爱的活动；强调努力，而 courtship 也可指那段时间。

entries.definition: A show put on to be seen; in biology a courtship display is one part of courtship.
entries.definitionCN: 为被看见而做的展示；在生物学中，求偶展示是求偶的一部分。

entries.definition: Playful romantic attention without a promise of union; courtship implies a serious aim.
entries.definitionCN: 不带结合承诺的轻佻浪漫关注；courtship 含有认真目标。

entries.definition: The act or period of pairing for reproduction; it follows courtship and is not the same as it.
entries.definitionCN: 为繁殖而配对的行为或时期；位于求偶之后，并不等同于求偶。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: court + -ship: the state or art of paying court.
normal.cn: court + -ship：处于「奉承、争取」之中的状态或技艺。

normal.en: The family runs court, courtship, courteous, courtier, courtesy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 court、courtship、courteous、courtier、courtesy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: courtship display, courtship behavior, during courtship, courtship rituals.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：求偶展示、求偶行为、在求偶期间、求偶仪式。

normal.en: The oldest sense is the behaviour of a courtier, not of a lover.
normal.cn: 最古老的意思是在朝臣的举止，而非恋人的举止。

normal.en: Courtship precedes mating; the two words name different stages.
normal.cn: 求偶先于交配；两个词命名不同阶段。

abstract.en: Picture a fan of feathers opened like a letter written only to one reader.
abstract.cn: 想象一把羽毛扇展开，像一封只写给一个读者的信。

abstract.en: Picture a gift that costs the giver enough to prove the intention.
abstract.cn: 想象一份让给出者付出足够代价、从而证明意图的礼物。

abstract.en: Picture a book that slowly turns a stranger into a companion.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书慢慢把陌生人变成同伴。

examples.en: Their courtship began with letters and ended with a shared house.
examples.cn: 他们的追求始于书信，终于同住一个屋檐。

examples.en: The male's courtship includes a gift of a small fish.
examples.cn: 雄性的求偶包括献上一条小鱼。

examples.en: The committee responded to months of quiet courtship.
examples.cn: 委员会对数月来低调的争取作出了回应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「court（宫廷/追求）+ ship（状态）」——像朝臣一样殷勤地争取对方好感 → 求爱、求偶

root: court（拉丁 cohors「围场、随从队伍」经古法语 cort）+ -ship（古英语 -scipe，表状态）；由「朝臣举止」引申为「求爱、求偶」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one approach: attention paid to win favour, then the time it takes, then the animal version, the scripted display, the gift, the political flattery, the campaign, and finally any art of winning over.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个接近动作：先是为赢得青睐付出的关注，再是所花的时间、动物版本、脚本化展示、礼物、政治奉承、争取活动，最后是任何赢得人心的技艺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a careful, repeated approach made to turn indifference into acceptance.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次周到而反复的接近，把冷淡转为接纳。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS DURATION: attention given, and the time that attention fills.
branches.cn: 动作与时长：付出的关注，以及这份关注填满的时间。

branches.en: BORROWED BY BIOLOGY: the human shape becomes a display with a fixed order.
branches.cn: 被生物学借用：人类的形状变成有固定次序的展示。

branches.en: COSTLY PROOF: a gift shows that the intention is not idle.
branches.cn: 昂贵的证明：礼物表明意图并非空话。

branches.en: FROM PERSON TO BODY: flattering a patron, then courting a bloc of voters.
branches.cn: 从人到机构：先奉承恩主，再争取一群选民。

branches.en: WIDEST SCOPE: any strategy for winning someone over.

senses.title: Relating to the study of ancient material remains
senses.titleCN: 与古代实物遗存研究有关
senses.definition: relating to the scientific study of past human societies through the objects, structures, and traces they left behind
senses.definitionCN: 与通过古人留下的器物、建筑与痕迹来科学研究过去人类社会有关
senses.example: The valley is protected as an archaeological zone.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷被划为考古保护区。
senses.why: Greek arkhaiologia joins archaeo- 'ancient' and -logy 'study'. The adjective adds -ical, so it names whatever belongs to that study: its methods, its sites, its evidence.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 arkhaiologia 由 archaeo-“古老的”与 -logy“研究”组成。形容词再加 -ical，因此它命名一切属于这门研究的东西：方法、遗址、证据。

senses.title: Pertaining to the remains themselves
senses.titleCN: 指遗存本身：地下的器物与痕迹
senses.definition: of or concerning the physical remains of past human activity, rather than the written account of it
senses.definitionCN: 指或关于过去人类活动的实物遗存，而非关于它的书面记述
senses.example: Archaeological evidence shows that the village burned twice.
senses.exampleCN: 考古证据表明这个村庄曾两次被烧毁。
senses.why: The study and its objects are named as one: what archaeologists deal with becomes 'archaeological material'. The adjective shifts from the discipline to the things that feed it.
senses.whyCN: 研究与研究对象被用同一个名字：考古学家处理的东西成了“考古材料”。形容词从学科转到喂养这门学科实物。

senses.title: Belonging to ancient history as a subject
senses.titleCN: 属于作为学科对象的古代史
senses.definition: in the older sense, relating to the written or literary study of ancient history, before archaeology became a field science
senses.definitionCN: 较早的义项：与古代史的书写或文献研究有关，那时考古学尚未成为田野科学
senses.example: In 1700, an archaeological lecture was a lecture on ancient history, not on a dig.
senses.exampleCN: 在 1700 年，一场“考古学”讲座其实是古代史讲座，而不是关于发掘的讲座。
senses.why: Archaeology entered English c.1600 meaning 'ancient history'. The adjective could therefore describe bookish ancient history, long before the 1825 sense of a scientific study of peoples and civilizations.
senses.whyCN: archaeology 约 1600 年进入英语时意为“古代史”。因此这个形容词可以描述书斋式的古代史研究，远早于 1825 年才出现的“对民族与文明进行科学研究”的义项。

senses.title: Relating to field excavation
senses.definition: relating to the practical work of excavating, recording, and interpreting a site layer by layer
senses.definitionCN: 与逐层发掘、记录和解读遗址的实地工作有关
senses.example: The archaeological dig was closed during the rainy season.
senses.exampleCN: 考古发掘在雨季暂停了。
senses.why: A study of ancient things must go to the ground to find them. The adjective attaches to the trowel, the trench and the layer, so 'archaeological' becomes fieldwork rather than library work.
senses.whyCN: 对古老事物的研究必须下到地里去找它们。形容词于是附着在铲子、探方与地层上，archaeological 也从书斋工作变成田野工作。

senses.title: Belonging to the academic discipline
senses.titleCN: 属于这门学科：系、课程与专业
senses.definition: relating to archaeology as an academic department, degree, or profession
senses.definitionCN: 与作为大学院系、学位或职业的考古学有关
senses.example: She is writing an archaeological thesis on coastal trade.
senses.exampleCN: 她正在写一篇关于沿海贸易的考古学论文。
senses.why: Once the study is organised into departments and degrees, its adjective marks membership: an archaeological thesis, an archaeological society. The root is the same; the referent is now the institution.
senses.whyCN: 当这门研究被组织成院系与学位，它的形容词就标记归属：考古学论文、考古学会。词根未变，所指变成了机构。

senses.title: Relating to a period or region: classical archaeology
senses.titleCN: 属于某一时期或地区：古典考古学
senses.definition: relating to a branch of the discipline defined by a period, region, or culture, such as classical or prehistoric archaeology
senses.definitionCN: 与按时期、地区或文化划分的学科分支有关，如古典考古学或史前考古学
senses.example: Classical archaeological methods differ from those used on prehistoric camps.
senses.exampleCN: 古典考古的方法与用于史前营地的方法不同。
senses.why: The modifier narrows 'ancient' to one stretch of the ancient past. The adjective still says 'of the study', but the study is now bounded by a period or a map.
senses.whyCN: 修饰语把“古老”收窄到古代中的某一段。形容词仍表示“属于这门研究”，只是这门研究被时期或地图圈定了。

senses.title: Relating to industrial remains
senses.titleCN: 与工业遗存有关：工业考古
senses.definition: relating to the study of factories, machines, and infrastructure from the industrial age, often standing or still in use
senses.definitionCN: 与对工业时代的工厂、机器与基础设施的研究有关，这些遗存常仍矗立或仍在使用
senses.example: An archaeological survey of the mill recorded every gear and chimney.
senses.exampleCN: 对这座工厂的考古调查记录了每一个齿轮和烟囱。
senses.why: The method of reading objects, not the age of the objects, defines the adjective. Industrial remains can be studied with the same layer-by-layer discipline, so 'archaeological' extends to the recent past.
senses.whyCN: 定义这个形容词的是“读实物”的方法，而不是实物的年代。工业遗存也能用同样的逐层方法研究，因此 archaeological 延伸到了近现代。

senses.title: Relating to submerged sites: underwater archaeology
senses.titleCN: 与沉没遗址有关：水下考古
senses.definition: relating to the study of shipwrecks, drowned settlements, and other remains lying under water
senses.definitionCN: 与对沉船、被淹没的聚落及其他水下遗存的研究有关
senses.example: Underwater archaeological work mapped the wreck before anything was lifted.
senses.exampleCN: 水下考古工作在打捞任何东西之前先测绘了沉船。
senses.why: The ancient thing is now under water, but the same 'study of ancient things' applies. The adjective travels with the method into a new environment.
senses.whyCN: 古老的东西现在在水下，但“对古老事物的研究”仍然适用。形容词随方法进入了新的环境。

senses.title: Metaphorical: digging through layers of thought
senses.titleCN: 隐喻用法：挖掘思想的层层堆积
senses.definition: used figuratively of an inquiry that uncovers the hidden layers and assumptions beneath a system of ideas
senses.definitionCN: 比喻性地指一种探究，揭开某个观念体系下面隐藏的层次与前提
senses.example: The book offers an archaeological reading of modern medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对现代医学做了一种考古学式的解读。
senses.why: The discipline's signature move is removing layer after layer to expose what lies beneath. Applied to ideas, archaeology becomes a metaphor for tracing how a system was built up, as in an archaeology of knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的标志动作是一层层去掉覆盖物，露出下面的东西。把它用到观念上，archaeology 就成为追溯一个体系如何层层堆积起来的隐喻，如“知识考古学”。

intro.en: Archaeological is archaeology plus -ical. Archaeology is Greek arkhaiologia 'the study of ancient things': archaeo-, from arkhaios 'ancient', plus -logy, from -logia 'study'. Arkhaios itself comes from arkhē 'beginning'. The -ical ending is -ic plus -al, a compound adjective suffix. The archaeo- element means 'ancient' and has nothing to do with archi- 'chief' in architectural.
intro.cn: archaeological 是 archaeology 加 -ical。archaeology 来自希腊语 arkhaiologia“对古老事物的研究”：archaeo- 出自 arkhaios“古老的”，-logy 出自 -logia“研究”。arkhaios 本身出自 arkhē“开端”。-ical 结尾是 -ic 加 -al 的复合形容词后缀。archaeo- 成分意为“古老”，与 architectural 中 archi-“首席”毫无关系。

items.en: Greek arkhaiologia meant 'the study of ancient things'. It joined archaeo-, from arkhaios 'ancient', with -logia 'study, discourse'.
items.cn: 希腊语 arkhaiologia 意为“对古老事物的研究”。它把出自 arkhaios“古老的”的 archaeo- 与 -logia“研究、论述”结合起来。

items.en: Arkhaios 'ancient' derives from arkhē 'beginning': the ancient is what belongs to the beginning. The second element is -logy, the study of a subject.
items.cn: arkhaios“古老的”出自 arkhē“开端”：古老之物就是属于开端的东西。第二个成分是 -logy，即对某主题的研究。

items.en: English archaeology first meant 'ancient history', borrowed from French archéologie (16c.) or directly from Greek. It was a bookish term, not yet a field science.
items.cn: 英语 archaeology 最初意为“古代史”，借自 16 世纪法语 archéologie，或直接借自希腊语。它是个书斋词，还不是田野科学。

items.en: Only in 1825 does archaeology come to mean the scientific study of ancient peoples and civilizations through their remains.
items.cn: 直到 1825 年，archaeology 才指通过遗存对古代民族与文明进行的科学研究。

items.en: Archaeologic is recorded in 1731 and archaeological in 1766, both built on archaeology. The ending -ical is -ic plus -al: -ic makes the relational adjective, -al completes and stabilises it.
items.cn: archaeologic 记录于 1731 年，archaeological 记录于 1766 年，二者都建立在 archaeology 上。结尾 -ical 是 -ic 加 -al：-ic 构成关系形容词，-al 补足并稳定它。

items.en: Modern branches such as classical, industrial and underwater archaeology all keep the same elements. Only the modifier changes; archaeo- still means 'ancient', while archi- in architectural is Greek arkhi- 'chief'.
items.cn: 古典考古、工业考古、水下考古等现代分支都保留同样的成分。变的只是修饰语；archaeo- 仍指“古老”，而 architectural 里的 archi- 是希腊语 arkhi-“首席”。

note.en: The first group contains one true root-alike and two traps: architectural has archi- 'chief', while archaic shares the ancient root but not the discipline. The second group separates archaeology from neighbouring studies.
note.cn: 第一组包含一个真正同根的词和两个陷阱：architectural 里的 archi- 是“首席”，archaic 虽共享“古老”词根却不指这门学科。第二组把考古学与邻近学科分开。

entries.definition: relating to architecture or building design. Its archi- comes from Greek arkhi- 'chief', not from archaeo- 'ancient'.
entries.definitionCN: 与建筑或建筑设计有关的。它的 archi- 来自希腊语 arkhi-“首席”，不是 archaeo-“古老”。

entries.definition: very old or old-fashioned, often deliberately so. It shares arkhaios 'ancient' but describes age or style, not the study of remains.
entries.definitionCN: 古老的；过时的，常指刻意仿古。它共享 arkhaios“古老的”，但描述年代或风格，而不是对遗存的研究。

entries.definition: a person who studies ancient remains. It is archaeology plus -ist, so it names the practitioner rather than the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 研究古代遗存的人。它是 archaeology 加 -ist，命名从业者，而不是形容词。

entries.definition: the study of human societies and cultures, including living peoples. Archaeology is one branch of it when remains are the main evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 对人类社群与文化的研究，也包括在世的人群。当主要证据是遗存时，考古学是它的一个分支。

entries.definition: the study of ancient life through fossils. It deals with organisms, while archaeology deals with human material remains.
entries.definitionCN: 通过化石研究古代生命。它处理生物，而考古学处理人类的实物遗存。

entries.definition: the study of the past based mainly on written documents. Archaeology works from objects and traces, especially where no texts survive.
entries.definitionCN: 主要依据书面文献对过去的研究。考古学从器物与痕迹入手，尤其在无文字留存的地方。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Greek archaeo- 'ancient' and -logy 'study', the 1731/1766 -ic then -ical formation, and the fixed phrases archaeological site and archaeological evidence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：希腊语 archaeo-“古老”与 -logy“研究”、1731／1766 年先 -ic 后 -ical 的构词，以及 archaeological site、archaeological evidence 等固定搭配。

normal.en: Archaeo- is 'ancient', -logy is 'study': archaeology is the study of ancient things, and archaeological is everything belonging to it.
normal.cn: archaeo- 是“古老”，-logy 是“研究”：archaeology 是对古老事物的研究，archaeological 则属于这门研究的一切。

normal.en: Arkhaios comes from arkhē 'beginning', so the ancient is literally what belongs to the beginning.
normal.cn: arkhaios 出自 arkhē“开端”，所以“古老的”字面上就是“属于开端的”。

normal.en: Archaeologic came first in 1731, archaeological in 1766: -ical is simply -ic plus -al.
normal.cn: archaeologic 先在 1731 年出现，archaeological 在 1766 年出现：-ical 不过是 -ic 加 -al。

normal.en: Archaeological site and archaeological evidence are the standard frames: a place to dig and the objects that speak.
normal.cn: archaeological site 与 archaeological evidence 是标准搭配：一个可供发掘的地方，以及会说话的器物。

normal.en: Architectural has archi- 'chief', not archaeo- 'ancient': an architect is a chief builder, not a student of ruins.
normal.cn: architectural 里的 archi- 是“首席”，不是 archaeo-“古老”：建筑师是首席建造者，不是废墟研究者。

abstract.en: A trowel removes one thin layer at a time: the past is read from the top down, and each layer is younger than the one below.
abstract.cn: 一把铲子每次刮掉薄薄一层：过去要从上往下读，每一层都比下面那层年轻。

abstract.en: A grid of strings divides the ground into squares: the same ancient thing can be located precisely by its square and depth.
abstract.cn: 用绳子把地面分成方格：同一件古物可以靠它的方号与深度被精确定位。

abstract.en: Broken pots are fitted back together: archaeology rebuilds a whole society from fragments that were never meant to be a message.
abstract.cn: 破碎的陶罐被拼回原形：考古学用从未打算传递信息的碎片，重建整个社会。

examples.en: The archaeological team found a wall under the car park.
examples.cn: 考古队在停车场下面发现了一道墙。

examples.en: Archaeological evidence suggests the harbour silted up slowly.
examples.cn: 考古证据表明这个港口是慢慢淤塞的。

examples.en: She joined an archaeological survey of the old iron works.
examples.cn: 她加入了对那座旧铁厂的考古调查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿凯奥勒吉扣」——阿凯（Ar-chae）在奥勒（O-le）的土层里一层层挖，吉扣（Ji Kou）把碎片拼成一只古碗 → archaeological 考古的

root: 源自希腊语 arkhaiologia“对古老事物的研究”：archaeo-（arkhaios“古老的”，出自 arkhē“开端”）+ -logy（-logia“研究”）；archaeological 是 archaeology + -ical。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of archaeological all hang on one act: removing layers to expose what ancient people left. From the discipline and its remains, the word extends to ancient history, field excavation, academic departments, period branches, industrial and underwater work, and finally to the metaphor of digging through ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: archaeological 的九个义项都挂在同一个动作上：揭开层层覆盖，让古人留下的东西露出来。从学科与遗存，它扩展到古代史、田野发掘、大学院系、分期分支、工业与水下工作，最后到“挖掘观念”的隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trowel lifting one thin layer of soil from a marked square.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把小铲从划好的方格中刮起薄薄一层土。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND INSTITUTION: the study itself, and its departments, degrees and professions.
branches.cn: 学科与机构：研究本身，以及它的院系、学位与职业。

branches.en: REMAINS AND FIELDWORK: the objects that are studied, and the digging that finds them.
branches.cn: 遗存与田野：被研究的器物，以及找到它们的发掘工作。

branches.en: ANCIENT HISTORY: the earliest bookish sense, before archaeology became a field science.
branches.cn: 古代史：最早的、书斋式的义项，在考古学成为田野科学之前。

branches.en: PERIOD AND WATER: branches narrowed by a period or a region, including submerged sites.
branches.cn: 分期与水下：被时期或地区收窄的分支，包括沉没遗址。

branches.en: INDUSTRY AND METAPHOR: recent remains read like ancient ones, and ideas read like layers of soil.
branches.cn: 工业与隐喻：近现代遗存像古代遗存一样被阅读，观念则像土层一样被阅读。

intro.en: Archaeological is archaeology + -ical, where -ical is the compound of -ic and -al that makes a relational adjective. Archaeology joins archaeo- 'ancient' and -logy 'study'. The same archaeo- stem gives archaeologist, archaeometry, bioarchaeology, archaeobotany, archaic and archaism.
intro.cn: archaeological 是 archaeology 加 -ical，其中 -ical 是 -ic 与 -al 复合而成的关系形容词后缀。archaeology 由 archaeo-“古老”与 -logy“研究”组合。同一 archaeo- 词干给出 archaeologist、archaeometry、bioarchaeology、archaeobotany、archaic 与 archaism。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek in origin, but New Latin coined archaeologia from the Greek compound, and Latin archaismus gave English archaism. Latin architectura is listed only to show the contrast: its archi- is 'chief', not 'ancient'.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源于希腊语，但新拉丁语用希腊复合词造出 archaeologia，拉丁语 archaismus 则给出英语 archaism。列入拉丁语 architectura 只为显示对照：它的 archi- 是“首席”，不是“古老”。

items.meaning: relating to the study of ancient material remains
items.meaningCN: 考古学的；考古的（-ical 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The archaeological record is thin in that valley.
items.exampleCN: 那个山谷的考古记录很单薄。

items.meaning: the study of ancient peoples through their remains
items.exampleCN: 考古学依赖细致的记录。

items.meaning: a person who studies ancient remains
items.meaningCN: 考古学家（-ist 表示从事该学科的人）
items.example: The archaeologist brushed the soil away by hand.
items.exampleCN: 考古学家用手刷去泥土。

items.meaning: from an archaeological point of view
items.meaningCN: 从考古学角度；在考古方面（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 这个地区在考古上尚未被勘探。

items.meaning: the scientific measurement and analysis of archaeological materials
items.meaningCN: 考古测量学；科技考古（-metry 表示测量）
items.example: Archaeometry dated the pottery to 1200 BCE.
items.exampleCN: 科技考古把这批陶器定年在公元前 1200 年。

items.meaning: the study of human and animal remains from archaeological sites
items.example: Bioarchaeology can reveal diet and disease.
items.exampleCN: 生物考古学能揭示饮食与疾病。

items.meaning: the study of plant remains from archaeological sites
items.meaningCN: 植物考古学（archaeo-“古老”+ botany“植物学”）
items.example: Archaeobotany found seeds of an early wheat.
items.exampleCN: 植物考古学发现了早期小麦的种子。

items.meaningCN: 古老的；过时的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 这首诗使用了古旧的拼写。

items.meaning: an old word or style kept deliberately

definition_zh: 模拟；仿真；模拟实验；假装；模拟装置
definition_en: the imitation of a real process or situation, often by a model or computer, for study or training
core_image: 一间飞行训练舱里，屏幕上是云层，座椅随气流轻轻抖动
scene: 这里指「模拟」。 Pilots train in a simulation before they ever fly the real aircraft.
sceneCN: 这里 simulation 指「仿真训练装置」（第 3 个义项：用模型复现真实操作环境以供练习）；飞行员先在模拟舱训练，再上真机。图中可辨识物件：驾驶舱、投影云层、操纵杆、教员台。

pos.zh: 模拟；仿真；模拟实验；假装；模拟装置（可数或不可数，指装置或一次实验时用复数 simulations）

senses.title: Imitating a process
senses.titleCN: 模拟过程：用模型复现真实运行
senses.definition: the imitation of the behaviour of a real system by a model, often a computer program
senses.definitionCN: 用模型（常为计算机程序）再现真实系统的行为
senses.example: The simulation reproduced twenty years of erosion in four hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这次模拟用四小时再现了二十年的侵蚀。
senses.why: Latin simulatio meant 'a copying or feigning', from simulare 'to make like', built on similis 'similar'; the noun begins as 'making something like'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 simulatio 意为「模仿或假装」，出自 simulare「使相似」，而后者基于 similis「相似的」；这个名词的起点是「使某物相像」。

senses.title: A model's run
senses.titleCN: 一次仿真运算：模型跑出的一组结果
senses.definition: one complete run of a model producing a set of predicted outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 模型完整运行一次所产出的一组预测结果
senses.example: We ran a thousand simulations to estimate the range of sea level rise.
senses.exampleCN: 我们跑了一千次模拟来估计海平面上升的区间。
senses.why: Countability arrived with computing: each run is a separate event, so the abstract noun became countable.
senses.whyCN: 可数性随计算而来：每次运行都是独立事件，于是抽象名词变得可数。

senses.title: A training device
senses.titleCN: 训练用仿真装置：可反复练习的假环境
senses.definition: an apparatus that reproduces conditions for practice or testing
senses.definitionCN: 复现某种条件以供练习或测试的装置
senses.example: The hospital bought a simulation for practising emergency births.
senses.exampleCN: 医院购置了一套用于演练紧急分娩的模拟装置。
senses.why: The abstract act turned into a concrete object: the thing that performs the imitation is called a simulation.
senses.whyCN: 抽象动作转为具体物件：执行这种模仿的东西就被称为 simulation。

senses.title: Pretending an emotion
senses.titleCN: 假装：做出并非真心的表现
senses.definition: the act of feigning a feeling or condition one does not have
senses.definitionCN: 装作拥有某种并不真正具备的情感或状态
senses.example: His grief was simulation, and everyone at the table knew it.
senses.exampleCN: 他的悲痛是假装的，桌上每个人都知道。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: simulatio in Latin covered feigning, and English kept it alongside the technical use.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：拉丁 simulatio 本就涵盖假装，英语把这个义项与技术义一并保留。

senses.title: Simulation in statistics
senses.titleCN: 统计模拟：用随机抽样近似结果
senses.definition: in statistics, generating random samples to approximate a distribution or probability
senses.definitionCN: 统计学上指生成随机样本来近似某一分布或概率
senses.example: Monte Carlo simulation estimates the integral without solving it.
senses.exampleCN: 蒙特卡洛模拟无需解出积分即可估计其值。
senses.why: Statistics uses imitation as a computational strategy: when the answer cannot be derived, it is acted out many times.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把「模仿」当作计算策略：当答案无法推导时，就把它反复演出来。

senses.title: Simulation of a physical system
senses.titleCN: 物理系统仿真：在方程中预演现实
senses.definition: in engineering and physics, solving a system's equations to predict its behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 工程与物理中通过求解系统方程来预测其行为
senses.example: The bridge design was tested by simulation before any steel was cut.
senses.exampleCN: 桥的设计在切任何钢材之前先经过仿真测试。
senses.why: Engineering extended the word to numerical prediction: a cheap copy of the structure runs before the costly real one exists.
senses.whyCN: 工程把这个词延伸到数值预测：在昂贵的实物存在之前，先让一个廉价的复制品跑起来。

senses.title: Simulation of behaviour
senses.titleCN: 行为模拟：让智能体模仿真实行为
senses.definition: in social science and computing, modelling the actions of people or agents
senses.definitionCN: 社会科学与计算中，对人或智能体行为的建模
senses.example: The crowd simulation showed where bottlenecks would form.
senses.exampleCN: 人群模拟显示出瓶颈会在哪里形成。
senses.why: The object imitated shifted from nature to people: agents are given rules and their behaviour is acted out.
senses.whyCN: 被模仿的对象从自然转向人：给智能体设定规则，再演出的行为。

senses.title: Simulation as deception
senses.definition: a false appearance deliberately kept up to mislead
senses.definitionCN: 为误导而刻意维持的虚假外表
senses.example: The ceasefire was a simulation of peace that lasted three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 那次停火是一场维持了三周的和平假象。
senses.why: Feigning enlarged to public events: what is put on for show, without substance, is called simulation.
senses.whyCN: 假装扩大到公共事件：为展示而摆出、并无实质的东西，被称为 simulation。

intro.en: Simulation comes from Latin simulatio, from simulare 'to make like, to imitate', built on similis 'similar'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: simulation 出自拉丁 simulatio，源自 simulare「使相似、模仿」，基于 similis「相似的」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin similis meant 'like, similar'. It is well recorded, and it also underlies similis-based words such as resemble and similar; its deeper origin is disputed.
items.cn: 拉丁 similis 意为「相像的、相似的」。记录充分，也支撑 resemble、similar 等词；其更深来源有争议。

items.en: The verb simulare meant 'to make like, to copy, and also to feign'. The feigning sense was present from early on, which is why the noun carries both imitation and pretence.
items.cn: 动词 simulare 意为「使相像、复制」，也表示「假装」。假装义很早就存在，因此这个名词同时承载「模仿」与「作假」。

items.en: The noun simulatio covered 'a likeness, an imitation, a feigning'. Classical usage leans toward the negative, pretence.
items.cn: 名词 simulatio 涵盖「相似、模仿、假装」。古典用法偏向负面，即「作假」。

items.en: English simulation appears in the Middle Ages through French, first meaning 'pretence'. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 simulation 经法语于中世纪出现，初义为「假装」。最早确切书证年代存疑。

items.en: From the mid-twentieth century simulation became primarily technical: a model imitating a system, and later a device reproducing conditions for training.
items.cn: 自 20 世纪中叶起，simulation 主要成为技术词：模型模仿系统，后又指复现条件以供训练的装置。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation date only): the first English date is uncertain; the origin of similis before its 'like' sense is debated and any Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：英语首见年代存疑；similis 在「相像」义之前的来源有争议，任何印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: The first group holds same-family words that differ in part of speech; the second holds near-synonyms for imitation or for a model.
note.cn: 第一组是同族词，区别在词性；第二组是表示模仿或模型的近义词。

entries.definition: To imitate or feign. It names the act; simulation is the act as a thing or the device that performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 模拟或假装。它命名动作；simulation 则是作为事物的动作，或执行该动作的装置。

entries.definition: Describes something artificial made to resemble the real thing, as in simulated leather. It is a property, not a procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 描述为仿照真品而造的人造物，如 simulated leather。它是属性，而非程序。

entries.definition: The device that runs the imitation. Simulation can also mean the device, but simulator is the precise term.
entries.definitionCN: 执行模仿的装置。simulation 也可指装置，但 simulator 是更精确的说法。

entries.definition: Means 'alike'. It shares similis but makes no claim about imitation or modelling.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「相似的」。它同出 similis，但与模仿或建模无关。

entries.definition: A simplified representation of a system. A model is the thing used; a simulation is the running of it.
entries.definitionCN: 对系统的简化表示。模型是被使用的对象；模拟则是让它运行起来。

entries.definition: The act of copying something, often with the implication of inferiority. Simulation is neutral in technical use.
entries.definitionCN: 复制某物的行为，常含「次一等」的意味。simulation 在技术语境中是中性的。

entries.definition: Copying in order to equal or surpass. It carries rivalry, while simulation need not compete.
entries.definitionCN: 为追平或超越而仿效。它带有竞争意味，而 simulation 不必涉及竞争。

entries.definition: An exact copy or a repeated experiment. It stresses fidelity, while simulation stresses a working imitation.
entries.definitionCN: 精确复制或重复实验。它强调忠实度，而 simulation 强调可运行的模仿。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: similis 'similar' + -atio: making something like the real thing.
normal.cn: similis「相似的」+ -atio：把某物做得像真的。

normal.en: The family runs similar, simulate, simulated, simulation, simulator, dissimulate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 similar、simulate、simulated、simulation、simulator、dissimulate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: computer simulation, simulation model, flight simulation, run a simulation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：计算机模拟、仿真模型、飞行模拟、运行一次模拟。

normal.en: The same noun covers the act, one run, and the machine that does it.
normal.cn: 同一个名词既覆盖动作、一次运行，也覆盖执行它的机器。

normal.en: The Latin noun already meant 'pretence', which is why the word can still accuse someone of faking.
normal.cn: 拉丁名词本就含「假装」，因此这个词至今仍可用来指责作假。

abstract.en: Picture a cockpit on the ground, with clouds painted on a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一间留在地面的驾驶舱，云层画在屏幕上。

abstract.en: Picture a scale model of a bridge bending under tiny weights.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥梁的缩尺模型在小砝码下弯曲。

abstract.en: Picture an actor crying on cue, with no grief behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一名演员按提示落泪，背后并无悲伤。

examples.en: The climate simulation predicted a wetter winter for the region.
examples.cn: 这次气候模拟预测该地区冬季将更湿润。

examples.en: Medical students practise on a simulation before touching a patient.
examples.cn: 医学生在接触病人之前先在模拟装置上练习。

examples.en: Her calm was a simulation that lasted until the door closed.
examples.cn: 她的镇定是装出来的，一直撑到门关上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「simil（相似）+ ation（行为）」——做出相似的东西 → simulation 模拟、仿真

root: 拉丁 similis「相似的」→ simulare「使相似、模仿、假装」→ simulatio「模仿；假装」→ 英语 simulation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one imitation: something is made to behave like the real thing, and that copy can be a run of a model, a training machine, a statistical trick or a lie.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次模仿展开：某物被做得像真的，而这个复制品可以是一次模型运算、一台训练机器、一种统计手段，也可以是一句谎言。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cockpit on the ground with painted clouds and a shaking seat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间留在地面的驾驶舱，云层是画上去的，座椅在抖。

branches.en: TECHNICAL IMITATION: a model reproduces a real process, whether natural or engineered.
branches.cn: 技术模仿：模型再现真实过程，无论自然的还是工程的。

branches.en: COUNTED RUNS: each execution is a simulation, and random runs approximate an answer.
branches.cn: 可数的运行：每次执行都是一次模拟，随机运行可逼近答案。

branches.en: OBJECTS AND AGENTS: the device imitates conditions, and agents imitate behaviour.
branches.cn: 装置与智能体：装置模仿条件，智能体模仿行为。

branches.en: FEIGNING: the oldest Latin layer, where the copy is worn as a mask.
branches.cn: 假装：最古老的拉丁层，复制品被当作面具戴上。

branches.en: PUBLIC PRETENCE: feigning scaled up to events presented as real.
branches.cn: 公共假象：假装被放大为被呈现为真实的事件。

intro.en: Simulation is a Latin likeness stem with a verb-forming suffix and an action-noun ending.
intro.cn: simulation 是拉丁「相似」词干加动词化后缀与动作名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin similis 'like' gives simulare 'to make like'; -atio turns the verb into the action noun simulatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 similis「相像」产生 simulare「使相像」；-atio 把动词转为动作名词 simulatio。

items.example: The simulation took six hours to run.
items.exampleCN: 这次模拟运行了六小时。

items.example: The simulator logged every control input.
items.exampleCN: 模拟器记录了每一次操纵输入。

items.example: Similarity between the species is striking.
items.exampleCN: 这两个物种的相似性很惊人。

items.meaning: to hide one's feelings by pretence
items.example: He dissimulated his anger with a smile.

definition_zh: 巨石；史前建筑中使用的大块粗石；竖石、石棚等巨石建筑的构件
definition_en: a very large rough stone used in prehistoric structures; a standing stone or a slab of a megalithic monument
core_image: 荒野上立着几块竖石，围成一个半圆，石面被风雨磨得凹凸不平
scene: 荒野上立着几块竖石，围成一个半圆。 A single megalith stands at the entrance to the stone circle.
sceneCN: 这里 megalith 指「史前建筑中使用的大块粗石」（第 1 个义项：史前巨石）；句意为一块巨石立在石圈入口处。

pos.zh: 巨石；史前巨石建筑构件

derivatives.zh: megalith + -ic（形容词后缀）→ 巨石的；巨石建筑的
megalith + -ism（体系后缀）→ 巨石建筑传统
megalith + -ist（研究者后缀）→ 巨石文化研究者
megalith + -ic（再次构词）→ 与巨石遗迹有关的
「大」前缀 + sauros「蜥蜴」→ 斑龙：另一条「大」词根线

senses.title: A very large stone in a prehistoric structure
senses.titleCN: 史前建筑中的大块粗石
senses.definition: a large, roughly shaped stone used as a building element in prehistoric monuments
senses.definitionCN: 史前纪念建筑中用作构件的大块粗加工石头
senses.example: A single megalith stands at the entrance to the stone circle.
senses.exampleCN: 一块巨石立在石圈入口处。
senses.why: megas means 'great' and lithos means 'stone'; the word names the size of the block before its function.
senses.whyCN: megas 意为「巨大」，lithos 意为「石头」；这个词先命名石块的大小，再指其功能。

senses.title: A standing stone or menhir
senses.definition: a single tall stone set upright in the ground, often for ritual or memorial purposes
senses.definitionCN: 单独竖立在地面上的高石，常用于仪式或纪念
senses.example: The tallest megalith in the field leans slightly to the north.
senses.exampleCN: 田野里最高的巨石略微向北倾斜。
senses.why: the standing stone is the simplest form of the prehistoric large block, so the general term covers it.
senses.whyCN: 竖石是史前大石块最简单的形态，因此通称也覆盖它。

senses.title: A slab in a chamber tomb
senses.definition: one of the large slabs forming the walls or roof of a prehistoric chamber tomb
senses.definitionCN: 构成史前石室墓墙壁或顶盖的大石板之一
senses.example: Each megalith of the tomb weighs more than a small car.
senses.exampleCN: 这座墓的每块巨石都比一辆小汽车重。
senses.why: a tomb built of big slabs uses the same oversized stone unit, now as wall and roof.
senses.whyCN: 用大石板建成的墓使用同样的超大石块单位，只是用作墙与顶。

senses.title: An element of a stone circle
senses.definition: one of the large stones arranged in a ring or oval at a prehistoric site
senses.definitionCN: 史前遗址中排列成环或椭圆的大石之一
senses.example: Every megalith in the circle is paired with a gap or a sightline.
senses.exampleCN: 石圈中的每块巨石都与一个缺口或视线方向相配。
senses.why: a ring arrangement gives the stone a place in a pattern, so the unit sense becomes an element sense.
senses.whyCN: 环形排列给石头一个图案中的位置，因此单位义变成元素义。

senses.title: A class of archaeological monument
senses.definition: the category of monuments built from such large stones, studied as one archaeological class
senses.definitionCN: 由这类大石建成的纪念建筑类别，作为一个考古类别研究
senses.example: The survey records every megalith within the valley boundary.
senses.exampleCN: 这次调查记录了谷地边界内的每一处巨石遗迹。
senses.why: surveying turns single stones into a monument class, which is how the word works as an archaeological category.
senses.whyCN: 调查把单块石头归成遗迹类别，这就是这个词作为考古类别的方式。

senses.title: A rough massive block in ancient construction
senses.titleCN: 古代建筑中的粗大石块
senses.definition: a large rough block used in ancient walls or foundations, not necessarily prehistoric
senses.definitionCN: 古代墙体或地基中使用的大块粗石，不一定属于史前
senses.example: The fortification rests on megaliths laid without mortar.
senses.exampleCN: 防御墙建在不用灰浆砌合的巨石上。
senses.why: ancient walls reuse oversized blocks, so the term can describe construction stone outside a prehistoric monument.
senses.whyCN: 古代城墙重复使用超大石块，因此这个词也能描述史前遗迹之外的建筑石料。

senses.title: An immovable obstacle
senses.definition: a figurative use for something huge, stubborn and impossible to shift
senses.definitionCN: 比喻极其巨大、顽固、无法移动的事物
senses.example: The old rule sat in the code like a megalith in a field.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧规定像田野里的巨石一样杵在法典中。
senses.why: an immovable stone is the natural image for a rule that cannot be shifted.
senses.whyCN: 挪不动的石头，是形容无法撼动的规定的自然意象。

senses.title: A symbol of prehistoric culture
senses.definition: a shorthand image for the stone-building cultures of the Neolithic and Bronze Age
senses.definitionCN: 对新石器与青铜时代筑石文化的简称式形象
senses.example: The museum uses a megalith as the symbol of its prehistory gallery.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆用巨石作为史前展厅的标志。
senses.why: a single stone can stand for an entire building culture, a part-for-whole symbol.
senses.whyCN: 单块石头可以代表整个筑石文化，是以部分代整体的象征。

intro.en: Megalith is a modern scientific compound from Greek megas 'great' and lithos 'stone'. It was coined by nineteenth-century archaeologists who needed one word for the oversized stones of prehistoric monuments.
intro.cn: megalith 是近代科学复合词，由希腊 megas「巨大」与 lithos「石头」构成。十九世纪考古学家需要一个词来统称史前纪念建筑中的超大石块，于是造出此词。

items.en: Megas meant 'great, large', the first half of many scientific compounds.
items.cn: megas 意为「巨大、大」，是许多科学复合词的前半。

items.en: Lithos meant 'stone', the root behind lithograph and monolith.
items.cn: lithos 意为「石头」，是 lithograph 与 monolith 的词根。

items.en: The compound megalith was formed in English, not inherited whole from Greek.
items.cn: 复合词 megalith 是在英语中构成的，并非从希腊语整体继承。

items.en: Archaeologists adopted it for the large stones of dolmens, menhirs and stone circles.
items.cn: 考古学家用它指石棚、独石与石圈中的大石。

items.en: The word spread with the study of prehistoric monuments and produced the adjective megalithic.
items.cn: 随着史前遗迹研究传播，这个词又产出了形容词 megalithic。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact year of the first English use is given differently in different sources, though the Greek parts are certain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：各资料给出的英语首见年份不一，但希腊成分是确定的。

note.en: Group one holds stone monument types easily confused with a megalith; group two holds words for big stones and large scale.
note.cn: 第一组是容易与巨石混淆的石构遗迹类型；第二组是表示大石与巨大尺度的词。

entries.definition: A lone upright stone; a megalith may be part of a larger structure.
entries.definitionCN: 单独竖立的石头；megalith 可以是更大结构的构件。

entries.definition: A chamber tomb of upright stones capped by a slab; it is built from megaliths.
entries.definitionCN: 由竖石撑起盖石的室墓；它由多块巨石建成。

entries.definition: A single large block or a monument cut from one stone; it stresses unity, not prehistoric date.
entries.definitionCN: 单一大块石或由整石凿成的纪念物；强调整体性，而非史前年代。

entries.definition: Describing a structure or culture that uses megaliths; the noun names one stone.
entries.definitionCN: 描述使用巨石的建筑或文化；名词指一块巨石。

entries.definition: A large rock shaped by nature; a megalith is chosen and placed by people.
entries.definitionCN: 天然形成的大岩石；megalith 是人选并安放的。

entries.definition: A flat thick piece of stone or other material; a megalith may be a slab but is defined by size and use.
entries.definitionCN: 石头或其他材料的厚平板；megalith 可以是石板，但以大小与用途界定。

entries.definition: A built memorial; a megalith may be one stone within such a structure.
entries.definitionCN: 建成的纪念物；megalith 可以是这类结构中的一块石。

entries.definition: A gigantic figure or thing; it stresses overwhelming size rather than stone construction.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的雕像或事物；强调压倒性的尺寸，而非石构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Greek roots, the archaeological class and the real monument types.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个希腊词根、考古类别与真实的遗迹类型。

normal.en: megas is 'great' and lithos is 'stone': a megalith is literally a great stone.
normal.cn: megas 是「巨大」，lithos 是「石头」：megalith 字面就是大石。

normal.en: A menhir is one standing megalith; a dolmen is a tomb built of several.
normal.cn: 独石是一块竖立的巨石；石棚由数块巨石建成。

normal.en: Stone circles arrange many megaliths in a ring.
normal.cn: 石圈把许多巨石排成一环。

normal.en: Megalithic is the adjective, megalith the countable noun.
normal.cn: megalithic 是形容词，megalith 是可数名词。

normal.en: The word belongs to archaeology, not to geology.
normal.cn: 这个词属于考古学，而非地质学。

abstract.en: A megalith is a stone that people lifted before they had machines.
abstract.cn: 巨石是人们在有机器之前就抬起来的石头。

abstract.en: It is a decision made permanent in rock.
abstract.cn: 它是用岩石做成永久的决定。

abstract.en: A field of megaliths is a conversation with people who left no other voice.
abstract.cn: 一片巨石群，是与没留下其他声音的人进行的一场对话。

examples.en: The megaliths were moved into place without metal tools.
examples.cn: 这些巨石在没有金属工具的情况下被安放到位。

examples.en: Each megalith in the tomb was cut from local granite.
examples.cn: 墓中的每块巨石都取自当地花岗岩。

examples.en: The survey maps every megalith along the ridge.
examples.cn: 这次调查标出了山脊沿线的每块巨石。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mega（大）+ lith（石）」——大石头 → 巨石

root: 希腊 megas「巨大」+ lithos「石头」→ 近代英语复合词 megalith，由十九世纪考古学用于史前建筑的大块粗石；不是希腊语原有整词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one oversized stone: a building block, a standing stone, a tomb slab, a circle element, an archaeological class, an ancient wall block, a stubborn obstacle and a cultural symbol.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守着同一块超大石头：建筑构件、竖石、墓板、石圈元素、考古类别、古墙石块、顽固障碍与文化象征。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough block taller than a person, set upright in open ground by hands that had no machines.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块比人还高的粗石，被没有机器的手竖在空地上。

branches.en: BIG BLOCK: a prehistoric element and an ancient wall stone are the same oversized unit in different buildings.
branches.cn: 大石块：史前构件与古墙石块是不同建筑中的同一超大单位。

branches.en: UPRIGHT AND ROOF: a lone standing stone and a tomb slab are the vertical and horizontal uses of one block.
branches.cn: 竖与横：独石与墓板是同一块石的竖用与横用。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENT AND CLASS: a circle element and an archaeological category place the stone in a pattern and in a science.
branches.cn: 排列与类别：石圈元素与考古类别把石头放进图案与学科。

branches.en: IMMOVABLE WEIGHT: a stubborn rule borrows the stone's inability to be shifted.
branches.cn: 不可移的重量：顽固规定借用了石头挪不动的特性。

branches.en: PREHISTORY'S SIGN: the stone becomes a shorthand for an entire stone-building culture.
branches.cn: 史前的符号：石头成为一个整套筑石文化的简称。

intro.en: Megalith is a scientific compound whose two Greek parts also build several English words.
intro.cn: megalith 是科学复合词，它的两个希腊成分还构成若干英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed Greek megas as magnus in meaning, and Greek lithos as lapis in meaning; the compound itself is modern English, so Latin has no direct equivalent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在意义上以 magnus 对应希腊 megas，以 lapis 对应希腊 lithos；复合词本身是近代英语，因此拉丁语没有直接对应形式。

items.example: The second root names the material.
The compound names one large block.

items.meaning: the tradition of building with megaliths
items.example: Megalithism spread along the Atlantic coast.
items.exampleCN: 巨石建筑传统沿大西洋海岸传播。

items.example: A monolith is one block, not a class of monuments.
items.exampleCN: 独石是一整块石，不是一类遗迹。

items.example: The dinosaur name uses the same size root.
items.exampleCN: 恐龙名使用同一个「大」词根。

derivatives.zh: megalith + -ic（形容词后缀）→ 巨石的
megalith + -ism（体系后缀）→ 巨石建筑传统
megalith + -ist（研究者后缀）→ 巨石文化研究者
monos「一」+ lithos「石」→ 独石；整块巨石
